ARTICLE 5 — TERM AND TERMINATION

5.1 Initial Term. This Agreement runs for five (5) years from the Effective Date.

Regulatory frameworks to address: FINRA rules, Securities Act of 1933, Securities Exchange Act of 1934, FINRA Code of Arbitration Procedure, Regulation FD, insider trading laws. Distinctive features to include: Engagement Letter model with success fee contingent on Closing; tail period for success fees (12-24 months post-termination); non-exclusive engagement by default; no fiduciary relationship explicit disclaimer. Produce the complete agreement with all 15 articles in the standard ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS through ARTICLE 15 — GENERAL PROVISIONS structure. Do not summarize, do not abbreviate sections, and do not skip any clause.

INVESTMENT BANKING ENGAGEMENT AND ADVISORY SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Investment Banking Engagement and Advisory Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is made and entered into as of March 12, 2024 (the "Effective Date"), by and between Meridian SaaS Holdings, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "Advisor"), having its principal place of business at 1528 Park Street, San Francisco, California 205, and Granite State Banking Corp., a California corporation (the "Company"), having its principal place of business at 1749 Maple Street, San Francisco, California 206. The Advisor and the Company may each be referred to as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties."

The Company wishes to engage the Advisor as its non-exclusive financial advisor in connection with potential strategic transactions, including without limitation potential acquisitions, divestitures, mergers, recapitalizations, restructurings, and capital raises (each, a "Transaction"). The Advisor is a registered broker-dealer with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission and a member of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority ("FINRA"). This Agreement shall govern all engagements between the Parties pursuant to one or more Engagement Letters executed under this Agreement.

ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS

1.1 "Advisor Personnel" means the partners, managing directors, vice presidents, associates, and analysts of the Advisor and its Affiliates assigned to perform the Services.

1.2 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with another entity.

1.3 "Background IP" means any Intellectual Property Rights owned or licensable by a Party prior to the Effective Date or independently developed outside of any Engagement Letter, including the Advisor's financial models, valuation methodologies, deal databases, and proprietary research.

1.4 "Closing" means the consummation of a Transaction.

1.5 "Company Information" means any non-public information about the Company, its Affiliates, its business, its financial condition, its strategic plans, its customers, its suppliers, its employees, its intellectual property, and any potential Transaction, that is provided to the Advisor by the Company in connection with the Services.

1.6 "Confidential Information" means all non-public information disclosed by one Party to the other in connection with the Services, including Company Information.

1.7 "Engagement Letter" means a written letter executed by both Parties in respect of a particular Transaction or class of Transactions, which incorporates this Agreement by reference and which sets forth the scope of the engagement, the fee structure (including any retainer, monthly fees, and Transaction-based success fees), the Transaction parameters, and any matter-specific terms.

1.8 "FINRA" means the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority.

1.9 "Intellectual Property Rights" means all intellectual property and proprietary rights of any kind anywhere in the world.

1.10 "Services" means the financial advisory services to be performed by the Advisor for the Company under one or more Engagement Letters, including identification and evaluation of potential Transactions, valuation analysis, transaction structuring advice, negotiation support, and assistance with diligence, marketing materials, and Closing.

1.11 "Transaction Value" means the aggregate value of consideration paid, received, or implied in a Transaction, calculated as set forth in the applicable Engagement Letter.

1.12 "Work Product" means the financial models, valuation analyses, presentation materials, fairness opinions, and other tangible work product prepared by the Advisor specifically for the Company in connection with the Services.

ARTICLE 2 — SCOPE OF SERVICES

2.1 Engagement Letters. The Advisor shall provide the Services to the Company only pursuant to an Engagement Letter executed by both Parties. Each Engagement Letter shall describe (a) the scope of the Services for the relevant Transaction or class of Transactions; (b) the Transaction parameters (including potential targets, sizing, geographic scope, and timing); (c) the fee structure; (d) the term of the engagement; (e) any retention bonus or expense advance; and (f) any matter-specific terms.

2.2 Order of Precedence. In the event of any conflict between this Agreement and an Engagement Letter, this Agreement shall control as to the matters expressly addressed, except that the Engagement Letter may expressly modify any provision solely as it applies to that specific engagement.

2.3 Standard of Performance. The Advisor shall perform the Services with the diligence, skill, and judgment ordinarily exercised by experienced investment banking professionals at major investment banking firms.

2.4 Non-Exclusivity. Unless an Engagement Letter expressly grants the Advisor exclusivity for a specific Transaction or potential Transaction, the engagement of the Advisor shall be on a non-exclusive basis, and the Company may engage other financial advisors in connection with any Transaction.

2.5 No Fiduciary Relationship. The Parties acknowledge that the Advisor is acting solely as an arm's length contractual party and not as a fiduciary or agent of the Company. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as creating a fiduciary relationship between the Advisor and the Company, or between the Advisor and any shareholder, director, officer, employee, or creditor of the Company.

2.6 Reliance on Company Information. The Advisor shall be entitled to rely upon the accuracy and completeness of all Company Information provided to it by the Company without independent verification, and the Advisor shall have no obligation to verify the accuracy or completeness of any such Company Information.

2.7 Cooperation. The Company shall provide the Advisor with such Company Information, personnel access, and management cooperation as the Advisor reasonably requires to perform the Services, including reasonable access to the Company's senior management, accounting records, and data room.

ARTICLE 3 — DELIVERABLES AND ACCEPTANCE

3.1 Work Product. The Advisor shall deliver Work Product to the Company in accordance with the schedule set forth in the applicable Engagement Letter or as otherwise agreed.

3.2 No Acceptance Mechanic for Financial Advice. The Parties acknowledge that financial advice and valuation work are inherently judgmental and that no formal acceptance mechanic applies to the Advisor's Work Product. The Company may, however, request revisions to the Work Product, and the Advisor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to address the Company's reasonable comments at no additional charge.

3.3 Fairness Opinions. Where an Engagement Letter calls for the Advisor to deliver a fairness opinion, the fairness opinion shall be issued in the form of a separate written opinion letter and shall be subject to such customary opinion conditions, qualifications, and limitations as the Advisor's fairness opinion committee determines to be appropriate. The Company shall not represent or distribute the fairness opinion in any manner not expressly authorized by the opinion letter.

ARTICLE 4 — FEES AND PAYMENT

4.1 Fee Structure. The fee structure for each engagement shall be set forth in the applicable Engagement Letter and may include any combination of (a) an upfront retainer fee, (b) monthly retainer fees, (c) progress fees, (d) a success fee contingent upon Closing of a Transaction, and (e) discretionary fees agreed by the Parties.

4.2 Annual Aggregate Reference. The aggregate annual fees payable by the Company across all then-active Engagement Letters as of the Effective Date is approximately One Million Two Hundred Thousand United States Dollars ($1,200,000), included for reference only and depending heavily on whether any Transactions Close during the year.

4.3 Success Fee. Where an Engagement Letter provides for a success fee contingent upon Closing, the success fee shall be calculated as a percentage of Transaction Value as set forth in the Engagement Letter. The success fee shall be due and payable in cash at Closing, by wire transfer of immediately available funds. The success fee shall be earned and payable regardless of whether the Transaction is consummated with a counterparty introduced by the Advisor or otherwise, provided that the Transaction Closes during the term of the Engagement Letter or during the tail period set forth in the Engagement Letter (typically twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) months following expiration or termination of the Engagement Letter).

4.4 Tail Period. The tail period set forth in the applicable Engagement Letter shall apply to any Transaction that Closes after expiration or termination of the Engagement Letter with a counterparty (a) introduced to the Company by the Advisor during the term of the Engagement Letter, (b) with whom the Advisor had substantive discussions during the term of the Engagement Letter, or (c) included on a list of covered counterparties exchanged at the end of the Engagement Letter. The Advisor's success fee shall be earned and payable on any such tail-period Transaction.

4.5 Retainer Credit. Any monthly retainer fees paid by the Company shall be credited (in whole or in part as set forth in the applicable Engagement Letter) against any success fee payable upon Closing of a Transaction.

4.6 Expenses. The Advisor shall be reimbursed for reasonable and documented out-of-pocket expenses incurred in connection with the Services, including travel, due diligence costs, data room subscriptions, and outside counsel fees. The Company shall pay or reimburse such expenses promptly upon receipt of an invoice. Where the Engagement Letter provides for an expense cap, expenses shall not exceed the cap without the Company's prior written consent.

4.7 Payment Terms. Retainer fees and expense reimbursements shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice. Success fees shall be due and payable at Closing.

4.8 Disputed Invoices. The Company shall notify the Advisor of any disputed amount within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of the invoice and shall pay all undisputed amounts on time.

4.9 Taxes. Fees are exclusive of all taxes other than taxes imposed on the Advisor's net income.

ARTICLE 5 — TERM AND TERMINATION

5.1 Term of this Agreement. This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue for a period of one (1) years, unless earlier terminated in accordance with Article 13.

5.2 Term of Engagement Letters. Each Engagement Letter shall continue for the term set forth therein. Termination of an individual Engagement Letter shall not, by itself, terminate this Agreement or any other Engagement Letter.

5.3 Survival of Tail Period. Notwithstanding any termination of this Agreement or any Engagement Letter, the tail period set forth in Section 4.4 shall survive and shall continue to apply to any Transaction that Closes during the tail period with a covered counterparty.

ARTICLE 6 — KEY PERSONNEL

6.1 Engagement Team. Each Engagement Letter shall identify the lead Advisor Personnel responsible for the engagement, including the lead managing director and the deal team.

6.2 Replacement of Lead Personnel. The Advisor shall not replace the lead managing director identified in an Engagement Letter without the Company's prior written consent, except in the case of (a) the death or disability of the lead managing director, (b) the departure of the lead managing director from the Advisor, or (c) the resolution of a conflict of interest. In any such case, the Advisor shall propose a replacement of comparable seniority and experience within fifteen (15) days.

6.3 Conflicts of Interest. The Advisor shall conduct conflict checks in accordance with FINRA rules and the Advisor's compliance policies before accepting any engagement. The Advisor shall promptly notify the Company of any actual or potential conflict of interest identified at the time of engagement or arising during the engagement, and shall not proceed with the engagement without the Company's informed written consent or the resolution of the conflict in accordance with FINRA rules.

6.4 Information Barriers. To the extent the Advisor identifies a potential conflict between the Company's engagement and the Advisor's other clients or the Advisor's own proprietary trading or investment activities, the Advisor shall implement and maintain information barriers (including ethical walls and personnel separation) reasonably designed to protect the Company's Confidential Information.

6.5 Non-Solicitation of Personnel. During the Term and for a period of twelve (12) months thereafter, the Company shall not solicit or hire any Advisor Personnel who performed Services for the Company; provided, however, that this restriction shall not apply to general public employment advertising not directed at Advisor Personnel.

ARTICLE 7 — COMPANY INFORMATION AND CONFIDENTIALITY

7.1 Use of Company Information. The Advisor shall use Company Information solely for the purposes of performing the Services in accordance with the applicable Engagement Letter. The Advisor shall not use Company Information for the benefit of any other client of the Advisor, for proprietary trading or investment, or for any other purpose.

7.2 Disclosure to Advisor Personnel. The Advisor may disclose Company Information to its personnel and Affiliates who have a need to know in connection with the Services, who are bound by obligations of confidentiality at least as protective as those set forth in this Agreement, and who are subject to applicable information barriers. The Advisor shall remain responsible for any breach of this Agreement by such personnel or Affiliates.

7.3 Disclosure to Counterparties. The Advisor may disclose Company Information to potential Transaction counterparties only after such counterparty has executed a confidentiality agreement reasonably acceptable to the Company, and only as necessary to evaluate the potential Transaction.

7.4 Securities Law Compliance. The Advisor and the Company acknowledge that some Company Information may constitute material non-public information about the Company. The Advisor shall ensure that all Advisor Personnel who receive material non-public information are placed on the Advisor's restricted list and shall comply with applicable insider trading laws and Advisor's compliance policies regarding material non-public information.

7.5 Data Security. The Advisor shall implement and maintain reasonable administrative, physical, and technical safeguards designed to protect Company Information against unauthorized access, including encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access controls, and a documented information security program.

7.6 Compelled Disclosure. The Advisor may disclose Company Information to the extent required by court order or applicable law, or to FINRA, the SEC, or other regulators with examination authority over the Advisor, in which case the Advisor shall give the Company prompt notice (where legally permitted).

7.7 Return of Company Information. Upon completion of the Services or upon the Company's earlier written request, the Advisor shall return or destroy all Company Information in its possession or control, except that the Advisor may retain (a) one archival copy of the Work Product as required by FINRA recordkeeping rules, and (b) Company Information embedded in the Advisor's working files for the duration of the Advisor's records retention obligations under FINRA rules and applicable law.

ARTICLE 8 — INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS

8.1 Background IP. As between the Parties, each Party shall retain all right, title, and interest in and to its respective Background IP. The Advisor's Background IP includes the Advisor's financial models, valuation methodologies, deal databases, market intelligence, proprietary research, and presentation templates.

8.2 Ownership of Work Product. Work Product prepared by the Advisor specifically for the Company in connection with the Services shall be owned by the Company, subject to (a) the Advisor's right to retain copies for its own files in accordance with FINRA recordkeeping rules and the Advisor's records retention policies, and (b) the Advisor's right to use Background IP embedded in such Work Product for other clients and purposes. The Advisor hereby assigns to the Company all right, title, and interest in and to such Work Product, to the extent assignable.

8.3 License to Background IP. To the extent any Work Product incorporates the Advisor's Background IP, the Advisor hereby grants to the Company a perpetual, irrevocable, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use such Background IP solely as embedded in the Work Product and solely for the Company's internal use in evaluating, structuring, or consummating the relevant Transaction.

8.4 Restrictions on Use of Work Product. The Company shall not represent or distribute any Work Product (including any fairness opinion) in any manner not expressly authorized in writing by the Advisor.

8.5 No Implied Licenses. Except for the limited rights expressly granted, neither Party grants any rights or licenses to the other Party.

ARTICLE 9 — CONFIDENTIALITY

9.1 Confidentiality Obligations. Each Party shall (a) hold the other Party's Confidential Information in strict confidence; (b) use it solely for the purposes of this Agreement; (c) not disclose it except as permitted by Article 7 (with respect to Company Information) or by this Article 9; and (d) protect it with at least reasonable care.

9.2 Compelled Disclosure. The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to the extent required by court order or applicable law (or by FINRA, the SEC, or other regulators with examination authority over the Advisor), with prompt notice to the Disclosing Party where legally permitted.

9.3 Survival. The obligations in this Article 9 shall survive any expiration or termination of this Agreement for a period of five (5) years.

ARTICLE 10 — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

10.1 Mutual Warranties. Each Party represents and warrants that (a) it is duly organized and in good standing; (b) it has the corporate authority to enter into this Agreement; and (c) this Agreement constitutes a binding obligation enforceable against it.

10.2 Advisor Warranties. The Advisor represents, warrants, and covenants that (a) the Advisor is duly registered as a broker-dealer with the SEC and is a member in good standing of FINRA; (b) the Advisor is not currently the subject of any FINRA or SEC enforcement action that materially affects its ability to perform under this Agreement; (c) the Services shall be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with the standards of the investment banking industry; and (d) the Advisor shall comply with FINRA rules, the Securities Act of 1933, the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, and all other applicable securities laws and regulations in performing the Services.

10.3 Company Warranties. The Company represents and warrants that (a) the Company has the right to engage the Advisor and (b) the Company Information provided to the Advisor is accurate and complete in all material respects to the best of the Company's knowledge.

10.4 Disclaimer. EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 10, THE SERVICES AND WORK PRODUCT ARE PROVIDED ON THE BASIS OF THE ADVISOR'S PROFESSIONAL JUDGMENT AND THE INFORMATION PROVIDED BY THE COMPANY. THE ADVISOR DOES NOT WARRANT THE OCCURRENCE OF ANY TRANSACTION, ANY SPECIFIC TRANSACTION VALUE, ANY SPECIFIC TIMING, OR ANY OTHER OUTCOME. THE ADVISOR DOES NOT WARRANT THE ACCURACY OR COMPLETENESS OF ANY COMPANY INFORMATION ON WHICH IT RELIES.

ARTICLE 11 — INDEMNIFICATION

11.1 Company Indemnity. To the extent permitted by applicable law, the Company shall indemnify and hold harmless the Advisor and its Affiliates and their respective directors, officers, employees, agents, and shareholders (each an "Indemnified Party") against any losses, claims, damages, liabilities, or expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by such Indemnified Party arising out of or relating to the Services or this Agreement, except to the extent any such loss, claim, damage, liability, or expense results from the gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud of the Indemnified Party.

11.2 Limitation on Company Indemnity. Notwithstanding Section 11.1, the Company's indemnification obligation shall not extend to any losses arising from (a) the Advisor's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud; (b) the Advisor's violation of FINRA rules or applicable securities laws; (c) the Advisor's breach of this Agreement; or (d) any liability that, under applicable law, the Company is not permitted to indemnify.

11.3 Contribution. If the indemnification provided in this Article 11 is unavailable for any reason, then in lieu of indemnification, the Company and the Advisor shall contribute to the losses in such proportion as is appropriate to reflect the relative benefits received and the relative fault of the Parties.

11.4 Indemnification Procedure. The Indemnified Party shall (a) provide prompt written notice to the Company; (b) cooperate with the Company in the defense and settlement of the claim; and (c) not enter into any settlement without the Company's prior written consent. The Company shall have the right (but not the obligation) to assume the defense of any claim with counsel reasonably acceptable to the Indemnified Party.

ARTICLE 12 — LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

12.1 Aggregate Cap. EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN SECTION 12.3, IN NO EVENT SHALL THE AGGREGATE LIABILITY OF THE ADVISOR ARISING OUT OF OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT OR ANY ENGAGEMENT LETTER, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), OR ANY OTHER LEGAL OR EQUITABLE THEORY, EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE TOTAL FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY THE COMPANY TO THE ADVISOR UNDER THE AFFECTED ENGAGEMENT LETTER DURING THE twelve (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO LIABILITY, OR (B) ANY APPLICABLE INSURANCE COVERAGE PROCEEDS RECEIVED BY THE ADVISOR.

12.2 Exclusion of Indirect Damages. EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN SECTION 12.3, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION DAMAGES FOR LOST PROFITS, LOST OPPORTUNITY, OR LOST TRANSACTION VALUE, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT.

12.3 Exceptions to Limitations. The limitations in Sections 12.1 and 12.2 shall not apply to (a) the Company's payment obligations, including any success fee payable upon Closing; (b) any breach of Article 9 (Confidentiality) or Article 7 (Company Information and Confidentiality); (c) any liability arising from a Party's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud; (d) any liability arising from the Advisor's violation of FINRA rules or applicable securities laws; or (e) any liability that, under applicable law, cannot be limited.

12.4 Basis of the Bargain. The limitations of liability are an essential element of the bargain between the Parties.

ARTICLE 13 — TERMINATION

13.1 Termination for Material Breach. Either Party may terminate this Agreement, or any Engagement Letter, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice if the other Party commits a material breach and fails to cure such breach within the notice period.

13.2 Termination for Convenience. Either Party may terminate this Agreement, or any Engagement Letter, for convenience at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice. Notwithstanding such termination, (a) the Company shall remain obligated to pay any retainer fees and expense reimbursements that have accrued through the effective date of termination, and (b) the Advisor's right to a success fee in respect of any Transaction that Closes during the tail period set forth in the applicable Engagement Letter shall survive termination.

13.3 Termination for Insolvency. Either Party may terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice if the other Party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, files a voluntary petition in bankruptcy, or has an involuntary petition filed against it that is not dismissed within sixty (60) days.

13.4 Effects of Termination. Upon expiration or termination: (a) the Advisor shall promptly cease performance of the Services; (b) the Advisor shall return Company Information in accordance with Section 7.7; (c) the Company shall pay the Advisor for all undisputed Fees and expenses that have accrued; (d) the tail period for success fees shall continue to apply as set forth in the applicable Engagement Letter; (e) each Party shall return or destroy the other Party's Confidential Information; and (f) the provisions that by their nature are intended to survive (including Articles 1, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, and 14) shall so survive.

ARTICLE 14 — GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

14.1 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of California, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles.

14.2 Venue and Jurisdiction. Any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be brought exclusively in the state or federal courts located in San Francisco County, California.

14.3 FINRA Arbitration Carve-Out. Notwithstanding Section 14.2, any dispute that is required to be arbitrated under FINRA rules shall be resolved by FINRA arbitration in accordance with the FINRA Code of Arbitration Procedure.

14.4 Informal Dispute Resolution. Before initiating any litigation or arbitration, the Parties shall attempt in good faith to resolve any dispute through direct negotiation between executives.

14.5 Waiver of Jury Trial. EACH PARTY HEREBY WAIVES ANY RIGHT IT MAY HAVE TO A TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY LEGAL PROCEEDING ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT.

ARTICLE 15 — GENERAL PROVISIONS

15.1 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, together with all Engagement Letters, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties.

15.2 Amendments. No amendment shall be effective unless in writing executed by both Parties.

15.3 Severability. If any provision is held to be unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force.

15.4 Waiver. No failure or delay in exercising any right shall operate as a waiver thereof.

15.5 Notices. Formal notices shall be in writing and delivered to the addresses set forth in the applicable Engagement Letter.

15.6 Independent Contractors. The Advisor is an independent contractor of the Company and is not a fiduciary or agent of the Company.

15.7 Subcontractors. The Advisor shall not subcontract any of the Services to any third party (other than its Affiliates) without the Company's prior written consent.

15.8 Assignment. Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party.

15.9 Force Majeure. Neither Party shall be liable for delays caused by events outside its reasonable control (other than payment obligations).

15.10 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts.

15.11 Headings. Headings are for convenience of reference only.

This is the TastePilot Customer Agreement (the "Agreement"). It is between Meridian SaaS Holdings, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "Provider," "we," "our"), and Forge Industrial Holdings Inc., a Florida corporation (the "Customer," "you"). It starts on April 22, 2025.

TastePilot is a hosted online ordering and customer engagement platform for multi-location restaurant groups. We try to keep our paperwork short and human. If something is unclear, email us at legal@tastepilot.com.

ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS

1.1 The "Service" is the TastePilot hosted online ordering platform — your branded ordering web page, the mobile app, the third-party delivery integrations, the loyalty program engine, the customer database, the analytics dashboards, the marketing campaign tools, and any updates we ship.

1.2 "Customer Data" is everything you put into the Service: your menu, your pricing, your locations, your customer database, your loyalty members, your order history, your campaign content, and any analytics you generate.

1.3 "Diner" is an end customer of yours who places an order through the Service.

1.4 "Diner Personal Data" is information about a Diner that the Service collects in the course of an order — name, email address, phone number, delivery address, payment method (tokenized), order history, loyalty membership, and dietary preferences.

1.5 "Locations" are the restaurant locations you operate that use the Service. The number of Locations covered by your subscription is set on the order confirmation email or in the dashboard.

1.6 "Third-Party Delivery Marketplace" is a third-party food delivery service (such as DoorDash, Uber Eats, or Grubhub) that we integrate with so that orders placed on the marketplace flow into your TastePilot dashboard.

ARTICLE 2 — SUBSCRIPTION AND LICENSE

2.1 What you get. We give you a non-exclusive license to use the Service for the Locations on your subscription during the Term. You can take orders through your branded ordering page, your mobile app, integrated Third-Party Delivery Marketplaces, and any other channel we add.

2.2 Authorized Users. Add as many of your team members as you need. You are responsible for what they do.

2.3 What you cannot do. You cannot reverse engineer the Service, build a competing online ordering platform with it, take orders for any restaurant that is not yours, or use the Service to send marketing messages without proper consent.

2.4 Suspension. We will give you a heads-up before suspending you, except in a security emergency. Reasons we might suspend: you are abusing the Service, you owe us money for more than 30 days, we receive a credible report that you are using the Service without proper consent for marketing messages, or a court tells us to.

ARTICLE 3 — IMPLEMENTATION

3.1 Onboarding. We help you import your menu, set up your branded ordering page, configure your locations, integrate with your existing point-of-sale system, and connect your Third-Party Delivery Marketplace accounts. Most customers go live in 7 to 14 days.

3.2 Onboarding fee. There is a one-time onboarding fee of Two Thousand Five Hundred United States Dollars ($2,500), waived if you sign a multi-year subscription.

3.3 Your part. You give us your menu data in a clean format, designate a project lead at each location, and respond to our questions in a reasonable time.

3.4 Done. Onboarding is "done" when your branded ordering page is live, your point-of-sale integration is sending orders to your terminals, and you can take a test order from start to finish.

ARTICLE 4 — FEES AND PAYMENT

4.1 Subscription. You pay Ninety-Six Thousand United States Dollars ($96,000) per year for the Service across the Locations on your subscription, billed annually in advance.

4.2 Per-order fee. In addition to the subscription fee, we charge a small per-order fee for orders placed through your branded ordering page: nineteen cents ($0.19) per order. The per-order fee is billed monthly in arrears.

4.3 Third-Party Delivery Marketplace orders. Orders that flow into the Service from a Third-Party Delivery Marketplace are not subject to the per-order fee in Section 4.2 — those are subject to the marketplace's own commission, which you pay directly to the marketplace under your separate agreement with them.

4.4 Adding Locations. If you add a Location mid-year, the prorated subscription fee is charged at the time you add it. If you remove a Location mid-year, the unused portion is not refunded.

4.5 Net 30. Annual fees are due 30 days after the invoice date. Monthly per-order invoices are due 30 days after the invoice date. Late payments accrue 1% per month or the most the law allows, whichever is less.

4.6 Renewal pricing. We may change the price at renewal. We will email you 60 days before any change.

4.7 Disputes. If you think a charge is wrong, dispute it in the dashboard within 30 days. Pay the parts you do not dispute on time.

4.8 Taxes. Fees do not include taxes. You are responsible for any taxes that apply.

ARTICLE 5 — TERM AND RENEWAL

5.1 Initial Term. The initial term is two (2) years, starting on the Effective Date.

5.2 Renewal. The Agreement auto-renews for one (1) year periods after the initial term. Either of us can stop renewal by giving written notice at least one hundred eighty (180) days before the current term ends.

5.3 You can cancel any time. Cancel in the dashboard. Cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing period.

ARTICLE 6 — SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SUPPORT

6.1 Uptime. We aim for 99.9% monthly uptime — meaning Diners can browse your menu, place orders, and pay.

6.2 Excluded downtime. Scheduled maintenance announced 48 hours ahead, your Wi-Fi or POS connection issues, Third-Party Delivery Marketplace outages, force majeure events, and your tier limits being exceeded do not count.

6.3 Service credits. If we miss the uptime SLA in any month, you get a service credit equal to 10% of one twelfth of the annual subscription fee. The credit applies to your next invoice.

6.4 Severity 1 incidents. We treat any incident that prevents Diners from placing orders during your operating hours as Severity 1, with a 30-minute first response target.

6.5 Support. Email support is included with a 4-business-hour first response target, Monday through Friday 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Eastern Time. After-hours emergency support is available for Severity 1 incidents. Phone support is available on the Pro tier.

6.6 Maintenance. We do routine maintenance on Tuesday mornings from 4:00 a.m. to 6:00 a.m. Eastern Time, when restaurant traffic is at its lowest.

ARTICLE 7 — YOUR DATA, DINER PRIVACY, AND CONSENT

7.1 You own Customer Data. You retain all rights to Customer Data, including your customer database and your loyalty member list.

7.2 Why we touch Customer Data. We host, store, process, and use Customer Data only to provide the Service to you — running your ordering page, processing orders, sending order confirmations to Diners, running your loyalty program, sending marketing messages on your behalf to Diners who have opted in, and computing analytics for you.

7.3 No selling, no AI training. We will not sell Customer Data or Diner Personal Data. We will not share Customer Data or Diner Personal Data with any third party except as needed to operate the Service (such as our payment processor and our SMS provider). We will not use Customer Data or Diner Personal Data to train any artificial intelligence model unless you give us specific written permission.

7.4 Diner consent is on you. You promise that for every Diner in your customer database who receives marketing messages from the Service, you have a lawful basis to send them messages — including under CAN-SPAM (15 U.S.C. § 7701), the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (47 U.S.C. § 227), and applicable state privacy laws. The Service supports unsubscribe links in every marketing email and a STOP keyword for SMS, but the legal obligation to comply with consent and opt-out rules is yours.

7.5 Loyalty data. The customer database and the loyalty member list are your property. If you cancel the Service, you can export them in standard formats (CSV, JSON) at any time. We will not retain them after the deletion period in Section 7.13.

7.6 Diner rights requests. If a Diner asks you to delete or export their personal data under an applicable privacy law (CCPA, CPRA, Virginia CDPA, Colorado CPA, Connecticut DPA, Utah CPA, etc.), you can use our self-service tools to honor the request. We will help on a reasonable best-effort basis.

7.7 ADA web accessibility. You acknowledge that your branded ordering page is subject to the Americans with Disabilities Act and applicable state accessibility laws to the extent it serves the public. We design the Service to substantially conform to WCAG 2.1 AA. You are responsible for any custom content (menu items, promotional content, custom HTML) you add through the dashboard.

7.8 Tenant isolation. Your Customer Data is logically isolated from every other customer's tenant.

7.9 Security. We protect Customer Data with TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest, role-based access controls, annual third-party penetration testing, and an annual SOC 2 Type II audit. Cardholder Data is tokenized at the point of capture by our PCI-compliant payment processor and never stored on our servers. We share the SOC 2 report under NDA on request.

7.10 Breach notification. If we discover a security incident that compromises Customer Data, we will tell you in the dashboard and by email within 72 hours of discovery.

7.11 Data residency. We host Customer Data in our United States region.

7.12 Subprocessors. The current subprocessor list is at tastepilot.com/subprocessors and includes our cloud hosting provider, our payment processor, our email sending provider, our SMS provider, and the Third-Party Delivery Marketplaces you have integrated. We give 15 days notice before adding or changing a subprocessor that handles Customer Data or Diner Personal Data.

7.13 Data export and deletion. You can export Customer Data through the dashboard at any time at no charge. After your account is canceled, we keep Customer Data available for 60 days. After that, we delete Customer Data within 30 days, with backup deletion completed within 90 days.

ARTICLE 8 — INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS

8.1 Our IP. We own the Service. The ordering platform, the loyalty engine, the dashboards, the SDKs, our trademarks, and any improvements are ours. Nothing in this Agreement gives you any of that.

8.5 No implied licenses. You only get the rights this Agreement actually gives you.

7.1 Ownership of Customer Data. As between the Parties, Customer shall retain all right, title, and interest in and to Customer Data. Provider acknowledges that Customer Data is the exclusive property of Customer.

7.2 Permitted Uses. Provider shall use and disclose Customer Data only as necessary to provide the Services to Customer in accordance with this Agreement and the applicable Order Form. Provider shall not use Customer Data for any other purpose, including without limitation product improvement, machine learning model training, marketing, or sale to third parties, except as expressly permitted by Customer in writing.

7.3 PCI-DSS Compliance. Provider shall maintain compliance with the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS) at the level required by the major card brands for the volume of card transactions processed through the Platform (which the Parties anticipate will be Level 1). Provider shall provide Customer with a current Attestation of Compliance from a Qualified Security Assessor on at least an annual basis and shall promptly notify Customer of any change in its PCI-DSS compliance status.

7.4 Cardholder Data Handling. Provider shall act as a "service provider" with respect to Cardholder Data within the meaning of PCI-DSS, and Provider's PCI-DSS compliance shall extend to all handling, storage, and transmission of Cardholder Data through the Platform and the Hardware Equipment. Provider shall not store any Cardholder Data outside of PCI-compliant scope. Cardholder Data shall be tokenized at the point of capture by the Hardware Equipment such that the Restaurant Location's network never transmits Primary Account Number information in the clear.

7.5 Brand Standards and Aggregate Reporting. The Parties acknowledge that the Brand Standards Module aggregates data across Customer's Restaurant Locations to compute brand-wide compliance metrics. Provider shall make this aggregated data available to Customer in the Brand Standards Module dashboard and reports, and shall not provide aggregated data identifiable to specific Restaurant Locations or Franchisees to any third party without Customer's prior written consent.

7.6 Security. Provider shall implement and maintain the safeguards required by PCI-DSS, including (a) encryption of Cardholder Data in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher; (b) encryption of Cardholder Data at rest using AES-256; (c) network segmentation isolating the cardholder data environment from other systems; (d) annual third-party penetration testing; (e) quarterly vulnerability scans by an Approved Scanning Vendor; (f) maintenance of SOC 2 Type II certification; and (g) a documented information security program reviewed at least annually.

7.7 Breach Notification. Provider shall notify Customer in writing of any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data without undue delay and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours of Provider's discovery. The notification shall include any information Provider reasonably has about the nature of the incident, the data involved, the affected Restaurant Locations and Franchisees, and the actions Provider is taking. Provider shall also notify the relevant card brands and acquiring banks as required by PCI-DSS.

7.8 Subprocessors. Provider shall maintain a list of subprocessors that have access to Customer Data on Provider's Customer Trust Portal. Provider shall provide Customer with at least thirty (30) days prior written notice of any addition or change to a subprocessor that has access to Cardholder Data. Customer may object to any new or changed subprocessor on reasonable security grounds.

7.9 Data Residency. Provider shall store and process Customer Data within data centers physically located in the contiguous United States.

7.10 Data Return and Deletion. Upon expiration or termination of an Order Form, Provider shall, at Customer's election, make Customer Data attributable to such Order Form available for export by Customer in a commercially reasonable, machine-readable format for a period of sixty (60) days, or permanently delete such Customer Data from production systems within thirty (30) days. Cardholder Data shall be deleted in accordance with PCI-DSS retention requirements.

This is the most important article in this Agreement, so we kept the language plain. If anything in this Article 7 conflicts with anything elsewhere in the Agreement, this Article 7 wins.

7.1 You own Student Data. The District owns all Student Data. We do not own it, we do not have any rights to it beyond the limited permission you give us in Section 7.2, and we will not claim a right to it later.

7.2 Why we touch Student Data. You give us permission to host, store, process, and display Student Data only to provide the BrightStep Platform to you. We will not use Student Data for any other purpose. Specifically, we will not (a) use Student Data to advertise or market to students or parents, (b) sell Student Data, (c) use Student Data to build user profiles for non-educational purposes, or (d) use Student Data to train any artificial intelligence model unless you give us specific written permission for a specific project.

7.3 FERPA. We are acting as a "school official" with "legitimate educational interests" under FERPA, 34 C.F.R. § 99.31(a)(1)(i)(B). That means we are subject to all the same restrictions on use and re-disclosure of education records that apply to your own employees. We will not re-disclose Student Data to anyone except the limited subprocessors we list at brightstep.com/subprocessors, and even then only as needed to run the BrightStep Platform.

7.4 COPPA. Many of your students are under 13. We rely on you to provide the parental consent that COPPA requires for school use, and we limit our collection and use of personal information from students under 13 to what is reasonably necessary for the educational service. We do not require students to disclose more personal information than is reasonably necessary to participate in an activity.

7.5 Ohio Student Data Laws. We comply with SOPIPA and AB 1584. We do not engage in targeted advertising, do not use covered information to amass a profile, and do not sell covered information. We will delete your students' covered information within forty-five (45) days of your written request.

7.6 Security. We protect Student Data with what we believe are reasonable security measures, including:
(a) encryption of Student Data in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher;
(b) encryption of Student Data at rest using AES-256;
(c) role-based access controls so only employees who need to see Student Data can see it;
(d) annual third-party penetration tests; and
(e) annual SOC 2 Type II audits, the report of which we will share with you under NDA.

7.7 Breach. If we discover a security incident that compromises Student Data, we will tell you in writing within seventy-two (72) hours, even if we are still investigating. The notice will tell you what happened, who we think was affected, what data was involved, and what we are doing about it. We will pay the reasonable costs of any breach notifications you have to send out under Ohio law if the incident was caused by something we did wrong. We will help your team investigate.

7.8 Where Student Data lives. We store Student Data in data centers inside the contiguous United States. We do not move it outside the United States. If we ever need to change that, we will get your written approval first.

7.9 Subprocessors. We use a small list of service providers (like our cloud hosting provider and our error tracking provider) that touch Student Data. The current list is at brightstep.com/subprocessors. We give you thirty (30) days notice before we add or change a subprocessor that handles Student Data, and you can object on reasonable security grounds. If we cannot resolve your objection, you can terminate this Agreement and get a prorated refund.

7.10 Audit. Once per year, with at least thirty (30) days notice, you (or a third party you choose, under NDA) can review our security practices. We will respond to a reasonable security questionnaire. For a deeper audit (like an on-site visit), we will charge you our reasonable costs and you will follow our protocols.

7.11 Data return and deletion. When this Agreement ends, you have ninety (90) days to export Student Data using our self-service export tool at no charge. After that, we delete Student Data from our production systems within thirty (30) days. Backups are deleted within ninety (90) days as part of our normal retention cycle. We will give you a written certification of deletion if you ask.

Each Statement of Work shall describe in reasonable detail (a) the scope of the Services; (b) the Deliverables; (c) the Key Personnel assigned; (d) the Fees and the basis on which they are calculated; (e) the schedule; (f) the acceptance criteria; (g) the location of performance; and (h) any project-specific terms.

2.3 Order of Precedence. In the event of any conflict between this Agreement and a Statement of Work, this Agreement shall control as to the matters expressly addressed in this Agreement, except that the Statement of Work may expressly modify any provision of this Agreement solely as it applies to that specific Engagement.

2.4 No Obligation to Engage. Nothing in this Agreement shall obligate Customer to engage Service Provider for any specific Engagement, and nothing in this Agreement shall obligate Service Provider to accept any specific Engagement.

2.5 Standard of Performance. Service Provider shall perform the Services in a professional and workmanlike manner, in accordance with the highest standards of the information technology services industry, by individuals possessing the qualifications, skills, and expertise required to perform the Services described in the applicable Statement of Work. Service Provider shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations in performing the Services, including without limitation the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, the Interagency Guidelines, the FFIEC IT Examination Handbook, and OCC Bulletin 2013-29 (Third-Party Relationships: Risk Management Guidance).

2.6 Onshore Delivery Only. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement or any Statement of Work, all Services shall be performed exclusively from facilities physically located in the contiguous United States, by personnel who are United States citizens or lawful permanent residents physically present in the contiguous United States. Service Provider shall not, without Customer's prior written consent (which Customer may grant or withhold in its sole discretion), perform any Services from, or provide any Service Provider personnel access to Customer Materials or Customer's regulated environments from, any location outside of the contiguous United States. This Section 2.6 is an essential term of this Agreement.

2.7 Cooperation. Customer shall provide Service Provider with such access to Customer Materials, personnel, facilities, and information as Service Provider reasonably requires to perform the Services. Service Provider shall not be responsible for delays in performance to the extent caused by Customer's failure to provide such access.

ARTICLE 3 — DELIVERABLES AND ACCEPTANCE

3.1 Delivery. Service Provider shall deliver each Deliverable in accordance with the schedule and in the format set forth in the applicable Statement of Work.

3.2 Acceptance Period. Customer shall have a period of twenty (20) business days following delivery of each Deliverable (the "Acceptance Period") to review the Deliverable and notify Service Provider in writing of (a) Customer's acceptance of the Deliverable, or (b) Customer's rejection of the Deliverable, accompanied by a reasonably detailed written description of the alleged non-conformity with the acceptance criteria set forth in the applicable Statement of Work.

3.3 Cure of Non-Conformity. If Customer rejects a Deliverable, Service Provider shall, at no additional charge, use commercially reasonable efforts to correct the alleged non-conformity and resubmit the corrected Deliverable to Customer within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of Customer's rejection notice. Customer shall then have a new Acceptance Period to review the resubmitted Deliverable. If Service Provider fails to correct the non-conformity after two (2) cycles of cure, Customer may, at its option, (a) accept the Deliverable in its then-current form with an equitable reduction in the Fees attributable to such Deliverable, (b) terminate the affected Statement of Work and recover any Fees paid for the rejected Deliverable, or (c) require Service Provider to engage at Service Provider's expense a third party reasonably acceptable to Customer to complete the rejected Deliverable.

3.4 No Deemed Acceptance. There shall be no deemed acceptance of any Deliverable. Any Deliverable not affirmatively accepted by Customer in writing shall remain unaccepted notwithstanding any passage of time.

3.5 Payment Tied to Acceptance. Service Provider shall not invoice Customer for any milestone-based or Deliverable-based Fees until the relevant Deliverable has been affirmatively accepted by Customer in writing.

ARTICLE 4 — FEES AND PAYMENT

4.1 Fees. Customer shall pay Service Provider the Fees set forth in each Statement of Work. The basis for Fees may include time and materials at the hourly rates set forth in the applicable Statement of Work, fixed fees, milestone-based fees, or any other basis the Parties agree to in the Statement of Work.

4.2 Annual Aggregate Reference. The aggregate annual Fees payable by Customer across all then-active Statements of Work as of the Effective Date is approximately Three Hundred Sixty Thousand United States Dollars ($360,000), included for reference only.

4.3 Rate Cards. Hourly rates set forth in any Statement of Work shall not be increased during the term of that Statement of Work without Customer's prior written consent. Rate increases for any new Statement of Work shall be limited to the lesser of (a) three percent (3%) above the rates in effect during the immediately preceding twelve-month period, or (b) the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U).

4.4 Expenses. Travel and out-of-pocket expenses incurred by Service Provider in performing the Services shall be reimbursed by Customer at cost, without markup, subject to Customer's then-current vendor travel and expense policy and accompanied by reasonable documentation. No expense in excess of Five Hundred United States Dollars ($500) shall be reimbursable unless pre-approved in writing by Customer.

4.5 Invoicing. Service Provider shall invoice Customer monthly in arrears for Services performed and expenses incurred during the preceding month. Each invoice shall describe the Services performed, the time spent (where Fees are based on time and materials), the personnel performing the Services, the Deliverables completed, and the expenses incurred.

4.6 Payment Terms. All undisputed invoices shall be due and payable within forty-five (45) days of the date of invoice, in accordance with Customer's standard accounts payable cycle.

4.7 Disputed Invoices. Customer may withhold payment of any disputed amount until the dispute is resolved. Service Provider shall not impose any late fee, interest charge, or service suspension with respect to any amount in good-faith dispute.

4.8 Audit Right. Customer shall have the right, upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, to audit Service Provider's records (including time records, expense reports, supporting documentation, and rate-card history) for any Services billed on a time-and-materials basis or any expenses billed under Section 4.4. If any such audit reveals an overcharge in excess of three percent (3%), Service Provider shall reimburse Customer for the reasonable costs of the audit in addition to refunding the overcharged amounts.

4.9 Taxes. Fees are exclusive of all taxes other than taxes imposed on Service Provider's net income.

ARTICLE 5 — TERM AND RENEWAL

5.1 Initial Term. The initial term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue for a period of five (5) years, unless earlier terminated in accordance with Article 13.

5.2 Renewal. Upon expiration of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive one (1) year renewal terms unless either Party provides written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the expiration of the then-current term.

5.3 Effect of Termination on SOWs. Expiration or termination of this Agreement shall not, by itself, terminate any Statement of Work that is then in effect, except as expressly provided in Article 13.

ARTICLE 6 — KEY PERSONNEL AND STAFFING

6.1 Key Personnel Designation. Each Statement of Work shall identify the Key Personnel of Service Provider who are committed to perform the Services under that Statement of Work. The Parties acknowledge that the identity, expertise, security clearance status, and continued availability of the Key Personnel are material considerations in Customer's decision to enter into the applicable Statement of Work.

6.2 No Replacement of Key Personnel Without Consent. Service Provider shall not remove, reassign, or replace any individual designated as Key Personnel on a Statement of Work without Customer's prior written consent, except in the case of (a) the death or disability of the Key Personnel, (b) the resignation of the Key Personnel from Service Provider, or (c) the termination of the Key Personnel by Service Provider for cause. In any such case, Service Provider shall propose a replacement of comparable seniority, expertise, and security clearance status within ten (10) business days, and Customer shall have the right to interview the proposed replacement and to reject any proposed replacement on reasonable grounds.

6.3 Key Personnel Service Credit. If Service Provider replaces any Key Personnel without Customer's prior written consent in violation of Section 6.2, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit equal to twenty-five percent (25%) of the Fees attributable to the affected Key Personnel during the month in which the unauthorized replacement occurred, and Customer may terminate the affected Statement of Work for cause without further notice.

6.4 Removal of Personnel on Customer Request. Customer may, at any time and for any reason that does not violate applicable employment law, request that Service Provider remove any individual personnel from the performance of the Services. Service Provider shall, within five (5) business days, remove the requested individual and propose a replacement of comparable seniority, expertise, and security clearance status.

6.5 Background Checks and Clearances. Service Provider shall ensure that all personnel performing the Services or having access to Customer Materials, Customer's regulated environments, or NPI shall have undergone, prior to commencing any work for Customer, (a) a criminal background investigation reasonably acceptable to Customer; (b) verification of work authorization in the United States; (c) verification of educational and professional credentials; (d) drug testing where permitted by applicable law; and (e) any additional security clearance, training, or certification reasonably required by Customer's vendor management policies. Service Provider shall maintain documentation of all such background investigations and clearances and shall provide such documentation to Customer upon request.

6.6 Citizenship and Residency Requirements. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, only Cleared Personnel who are United States citizens or lawful permanent residents shall be permitted to access NPI or Customer's regulated environments. Service Provider shall not assign any non-Cleared Personnel to any task that would foreseeably involve access to NPI or Customer's regulated environments.

6.7 Non-Solicitation of Personnel. During the Term and for a period of twelve (12) months thereafter, Customer shall not solicit or hire any Key Personnel who performed Services for Customer; provided, however, that this restriction shall not apply to (a) general public employment advertising not directed at Service Provider personnel, or (b) any individual whose employment with Service Provider has terminated for at least six (6) months prior to the date of solicitation.

ARTICLE 7 — CUSTOMER MATERIALS, INFORMATION SECURITY, AND REGULATORY COMPLIANCE

7.1 Ownership of Customer Materials. As between the Parties, Customer shall retain all right, title, and interest in and to Customer Materials, including all NPI. Service Provider acknowledges that Customer Materials are the exclusive property of Customer.

7.2 Limited License to Customer Materials. Customer hereby grants Service Provider a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free license to use Customer Materials solely as necessary to perform the Services in accordance with the applicable Statement of Work. Service Provider shall not use Customer Materials for any other purpose.

7.3 GLBA Compliance. Service Provider acknowledges that Customer Materials may include NPI and that Service Provider, in performing the Services, shall be subject to the obligations of a service provider under the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act and the Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards (12 C.F.R. Part 30, Appendix B). Service Provider shall implement and maintain administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to comply with such obligations.

7.4 Regulatory Examination. Service Provider acknowledges that Customer's use of the Services is subject to examination by Customer's Regulators under 12 U.S.C. § 1867(c) (Bank Service Company Act). Service Provider shall cooperate fully with any examination, audit, or inquiry by a Regulator with respect to Customer's use of the Services, including by (a) making available to the Regulator (and to Customer upon Customer's request) such books, records, personnel, facilities, and information as the Regulator may reasonably request; (b) responding to Regulator inquiries within the time frames required by the Regulator; (c) providing copies of Service Provider's SOC 1 Type II reports, SOC 2 Type II reports, and other relevant compliance reports as soon as available; and (d) permitting on-site examinations at Service Provider's facilities by the Regulator upon reasonable notice.

7.5 Customer Audit Rights. In addition to Customer's rights under Section 7.4, Customer shall have the right, upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, to audit Service Provider's compliance with this Agreement, the Service Levels, the security obligations of this Article 7, and applicable laws. Customer may conduct such audit using internal audit personnel or a third-party auditor of Customer's choosing, subject to such third-party auditor's execution of a reasonable confidentiality agreement.

7.6 Information Security Program. Service Provider shall maintain a documented information security program designed to comply with the Interagency Guidelines, the FFIEC IT Examination Handbook, and applicable industry standards. The program shall include at a minimum (a) administrative safeguards including written policies, employee training, background checks, and a designated information security officer; (b) physical safeguards including data center physical access controls; (c) technical safeguards including encryption of Customer Materials in transit (TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (AES-256), role-based access controls, multi-factor authentication for privileged access, and continuous monitoring; (d) annual third-party penetration testing; (e) maintenance of SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II certifications; and (f) annual independent assessment.

7.7 Security Incident Notification. Service Provider shall notify Customer's designated security contact in writing of any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Materials (a "Security Incident") without undue delay and in any event within twenty-four (24) hours of Service Provider's discovery. The notification shall include all available information about the nature of the Security Incident, the categories and approximate number of records affected, and the actions Service Provider is taking. Service Provider shall provide Customer with regular updates at intervals no less frequent than daily until the incident is resolved.

7.8 Breach Cooperation. Service Provider shall cooperate fully with Customer's investigation, response, and notification efforts with respect to any Security Incident, including by (a) providing forensic data and incident response personnel; (b) participating in Customer-led incident response calls; (c) reimbursing Customer for the reasonable costs of breach notifications, credit monitoring, and forensic investigation to the extent the Security Incident was caused by Service Provider's breach of this Agreement; and (d) cooperating with any Regulator inquiry arising from the Security Incident.

7.9 Subcontractors. Service Provider shall not engage any Subcontractor to access Customer Materials, NPI, or Customer's regulated environments without Customer's prior written approval, which Customer may withhold or condition in its sole discretion. Service Provider shall maintain a list of approved Subcontractors at a Customer-accessible vendor portal.

7.10 Data Residency. Service Provider shall store and process all Customer Materials only within data centers physically located in the contiguous United States.

7.11 Return of Customer Materials. Upon completion of the relevant Engagement or upon Customer's earlier written request, Service Provider shall return or destroy all Customer Materials in its possession or control, and shall provide Customer with written certification of return or destruction upon request.

OBSERVOLOOP — CUSTOMER AGREEMENT

This is the ObservoLoop Customer Agreement (the "Agreement"). It is between Pinnacle Digital Systems, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "Provider," "we," "our"), and Forge Industrial Holdings Inc., a Florida corporation (the "Customer," "you"). It starts on September 9, 2024.

ObservoLoop is a hosted observability platform — logs, metrics, traces, and alerts for software teams. We try to keep this Agreement short and human. If something is unclear, email us at legal@observoloop.io.

ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS

1.1 The "Service" is the ObservoLoop hosted observability platform — log ingestion, metric ingestion, distributed trace collection, the dashboards, the query engine, the alerting engine, the SDKs and agents, and any updates we ship.

1.2 "Customer Data" is the telemetry you send us — log events, metric series, distributed traces, span attributes, alert events, dashboard configurations, query history, and any source-attribution data your agents include.

1.3 "Authorized User" is anyone you authorize to log in to the Service.

1.4 "Ingest Volume" is the metered volume of telemetry your account ingests, measured in gigabytes per month for logs and traces and in active metric series for metrics.

1.5 "Sampling" is the practice of selecting a subset of telemetry events for ingestion, configurable in the agents and the Service dashboard.

ARTICLE 2 — SUBSCRIPTION AND LICENSE

2.1 What you get. We give you a non-exclusive license to use the Service for your software team during the Term. You can install our agents on as many of your hosts and containers as your tier allows.

2.2 Authorized Users. Your tier includes a number of Authorized User seats. Add more if you need them; they are billed at the per-seat rate on the pricing page.

2.3 What you cannot do. You cannot reverse engineer the Service, build a competing observability platform with it, send us telemetry that contains personal data without the right to do so, or use the Service to monitor systems you do not have permission to monitor.

2.4 Suspension. We will give you a heads-up before suspending you, except in the case of a security emergency. Reasons we might suspend: you are abusing the Service, you owe us money for more than 30 days, or a court tells us to.

ARTICLE 3 — IMPLEMENTATION

3.1 Self-serve. You install the agents on your hosts, point them at our endpoint, and start ingesting telemetry. There is no implementation phase. There is no setup fee on the standard tiers.

3.2 Onboarding help. We offer a free onboarding consultation for any customer that signs an annual subscription. Standard support handles ongoing questions.

ARTICLE 4 — FEES AND PAYMENT

4.1 Subscription. You pay Ninety-Six Thousand United States Dollars ($96,000) per year for your tier, billed annually in advance.

4.2 Volume metering. Your tier includes a baseline Ingest Volume. If you exceed the baseline in any month, the overage is billed at the rates on observoloop.io/pricing. Overages are billed monthly in arrears.

4.3 Sampling controls. You can configure sampling at the agent level and at the Service ingest endpoint to control your Ingest Volume. We offer guides at observoloop.io/sampling. We bill based on what you ingest, not what you generate, so good sampling can reduce your bill.

4.4 Volume alerts. We send a dashboard alert at 80% and 100% of your monthly baseline so you can adjust sampling or upgrade your tier before incurring overage.

4.5 Net 30. Annual fees are due 30 days after the invoice date. Late payments accrue 1% per month or the most the law allows, whichever is less.

4.6 Renewal pricing. We may change the price at renewal. We will email you 60 days before any change.

4.7 Disputes. If you think a charge is wrong, dispute it in the dashboard within 30 days. Pay the parts you do not dispute on time.

4.8 Taxes. Fees do not include taxes. You are responsible for any taxes that apply.

ARTICLE 5 — TERM AND RENEWAL

5.1 Initial Term. The initial term is one (1) years, starting on the Effective Date.

5.2 Renewal. The Agreement auto-renews for one (1) year periods after the initial term. Either of us can stop renewal by giving written notice at least thirty (30) days before the current term ends.

5.3 You can cancel any time. Cancel in the dashboard. Cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing period. We do not refund unused portions.

ARTICLE 6 — SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SUPPORT

6.1 Ingestion uptime. We aim for 99.95% monthly ingestion uptime — meaning your agents can successfully send telemetry to our ingest endpoint.

6.2 Query uptime. We aim for 99.9% monthly query uptime — meaning you can run dashboards and alerts against your ingested data. Query and ingestion are separate because we sometimes pause query temporarily during platform upgrades while ingestion continues normally.

6.3 Excluded downtime. Scheduled maintenance with 48 hours notice, your code (including misconfigured agents), third-party services we depend on, force majeure events, and your tier limits being exceeded do not count as downtime.

6.4 Service credits. If we miss the ingestion or query SLA, you get a service credit equal to (a) 5% of one twelfth of the annual subscription fee for any month between 99.9% and 99.95%, (b) 10% for any month between 99.5% and 99.9%, or (c) 25% for any month below 99.5%. Credits apply to your next invoice. They are the only money remedy for an SLA miss.

6.5 Support. Standard support is included: 24/7 access to the help center and ticketing portal, email support with a 4-business-hour first response target during business hours (Pacific Time), and 24/7 emergency on-call support for Severity 1 incidents (a complete production outage of your account) with a 1-hour first response target.

6.6 Maintenance. We do routine maintenance on Sundays from 11:00 p.m. to 2:00 a.m. Pacific Time. We give 72 hours notice for any other planned maintenance.

ARTICLE 7 — YOUR DATA AND PRIVACY

7.1 You own Customer Data. You retain all rights to Customer Data. We do not own it.

7.2 Why we touch Customer Data. We host, store, index, query, and serve Customer Data only to provide the Service to you — running your dashboards, evaluating your alert rules, and serving your queries. We will not use Customer Data for any other purpose.

7.3 No training. We will not use Customer Data — including your logs, metrics, traces, span attributes, alert payloads, or query history — to train any artificial intelligence or machine learning model. If we ever want to do anything else with your data, we will ask first.

7.4 No selling. We will not sell Customer Data, share it with advertisers, or include it in any commercial dataset.

7.5 Aggregate stats. Aggregate statistics do not identify you, your hosts, your applications, or any individual.

7.6 Personal data in telemetry. The Parties acknowledge that logs, traces, and span attributes may inadvertently contain personal data (user IDs, IP addresses, request headers, error messages with personal data in them). You are responsible for configuring your agents and your application to scrub or sample personal data before it leaves your environment. We provide configurable scrubbing rules at the agent and ingest level. The Data Processing Addendum at observoloop.io/dpa applies to any personal data we end up processing on your behalf.

7.7 Tenant isolation. Your Customer Data is logically isolated from every other customer's Customer Data.

7.8 Security. We protect Customer Data with TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest, role-based access controls, annual third-party penetration testing, and an annual SOC 2 Type II audit. We share the SOC 2 report under NDA on request.

7.9 Breach notification. If we discover a security incident that compromises Customer Data, we will tell you in the dashboard and by email within 72 hours of discovery.

6.1 Uptime Commitment. Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to make the Platform available with a Monthly Uptime Percentage of at least 99.5%, calculated as: (Total Minutes in Month - Excluded Minutes - Downtime Minutes) / (Total Minutes in Month - Excluded Minutes), expressed as a percentage. The Parties acknowledge that the Platform is designed to operate in offline mode at the terminal level for short periods of time, and that brief cloud connectivity interruptions affecting reporting and synchronization shall not generally affect order entry and payment processing functionality at the Authorized Locations.

6.2 Excluded Downtime. The following shall not be counted as Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, which shall be conducted between 3:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. Eastern Time and shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month; (b) emergency maintenance with as much advance notice as is reasonably practicable; (c) downtime caused by Customer's acts or omissions, including loss of internet connectivity at any Authorized Location; (d) downtime caused by Force Majeure Events; (e) downtime caused by failures of third-party services, including without limitation Payment Processors; and (f) downtime caused by Customer's use of third-party hardware that does not meet Provider's specifications.

6.3 Service Credits. If the Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below 99.5%, Customer shall be entitled to receive service credits as follows: (a) below 99.5% but at or above 99.0%: a service credit equal to five percent (5%) of one-twelfth (1/12) of the annual Subscription Fee; (b) below 99.0% but at or above 98.0%: ten percent (10%); (c) below 98.0%: twenty-five percent (25%). 6.5 Severity Levels. Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to resolve Severity 1 issues within two (2) hours, Severity 2 issues within two (2) business day, Severity 3 issues within five (5) business days, and Severity 4 issues per Provider's standard product roadmap. CLINICAL RESEARCH ORGANIZATION SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Clinical Research Organization Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is made and entered into as of August 5, 2024 (the "Effective Date"), by and between Streamline Cloud Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "CRO"), having its principal place of business at 9540 Commerce Avenue, 16th Floor, New York, New York 579, and Westhaven Therapeutics, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "Sponsor"), having its principal place of business at 1 Westhaven Therapeutics Center, Cambridge, Massachusetts 02142. This Agreement is subject to the United States Food and Drug Administration's regulations governing clinical investigations (including 21 C.F.R.
