ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS

1.1 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with another entity.

1.2 "Background IP" means any Intellectual Property Rights owned or licensable by a Party prior to the Effective Date or independently developed outside of any Work Order.

1.3 "Clinical Trial" means a research investigation involving human subjects designed to evaluate one or more biomedical interventions on health outcomes, sponsored by the Sponsor and conducted in accordance with applicable GCP principles.

1.4 "GCP" means Good Clinical Practice as set forth in ICH E6(R3) and applicable national regulations.

1.5 "ICF" means the informed consent form executed by each subject before participating in a Clinical Trial.

1.6 "Investigational Product" means the drug, biologic, or device being studied in a Clinical Trial.

1.7 "Investigator" means the physician or other qualified individual responsible for the conduct of a Clinical Trial at a particular site.

1.8 "IRB" means the Institutional Review Board (or equivalent ethics committee) responsible for reviewing and approving a Clinical Trial.

1.9 "Permitted Subcontractor" means any third-party subcontractor (such as a central laboratory, imaging vendor, or specialty CRO) approved by the Sponsor in writing to perform a portion of the Services on the CRO's behalf.

1.10 "Protocol" means the clinical study protocol approved by the Sponsor and the IRB for a Clinical Trial.

1.11 "Regulatory Authority" means the FDA and any analogous foreign regulatory authority with jurisdiction over the relevant Clinical Trial.

1.12 "Services" means the clinical research operations services to be performed by the CRO for the Sponsor under one or more Work Orders, including without limitation Clinical Trial design support, site identification and selection, site management, monitoring, data management, biostatistics, medical writing, regulatory submissions support, and pharmacovigilance.

1.13 "Site" means a physical location at which a Clinical Trial is conducted.

1.14 "Trial Data" means all data and information generated in or arising from a Clinical Trial, including without limitation case report forms, source documents, laboratory results, imaging, electronic health records data, biological samples (where applicable), and pharmacovigilance reports.

1.15 "Work Order" means a written work order executed by both Parties that describes a particular Clinical Trial or set of Services. Each Work Order shall reference and be governed by this Agreement.

ARTICLE 2 — SCOPE OF SERVICES

2.1 Engagement of Services. The CRO shall provide the Services described in each Work Order from time to time during the Term.

2.2 Work Orders. Each Work Order shall specify (a) the Clinical Trial(s) involved; (b) the scope of the Services; (c) the Protocol; (d) the deliverables; (e) the timeline and milestones; (f) the budget and Fees; (g) the Sponsor-approved Permitted Subcontractors; (h) the Sites and Investigators; and (i) any project-specific terms.

2.3 Order of Precedence. In the event of any conflict between this Agreement and a Work Order, this Agreement shall control as to the matters expressly addressed, except where the Work Order expressly modifies as it applies to the relevant Clinical Trial. Applicable law and regulation control over both this Agreement and any Work Order.

2.4 Standard of Performance. The CRO shall perform the Services in accordance with (a) the Protocol; (b) GCP and applicable Regulatory Authority guidance; (c) the CRO's standard operating procedures; (d) the standards of the clinical research industry; and (e) all applicable laws.

2.5 Sponsor Direction. The Sponsor retains overall responsibility for the design, conduct, and supervision of each Clinical Trial. The CRO shall act under the Sponsor's direction and shall escalate to the Sponsor any material decisions affecting the Protocol, the Investigators, the Sites, or subject safety.

2.6 No Subcontracting Without Sponsor Approval. The CRO shall not engage any Permitted Subcontractor without the Sponsor's prior written approval. The Sponsor may withhold approval in its sole discretion. The CRO shall remain primarily responsible for the performance of any Permitted Subcontractor and shall flow down to each Permitted Subcontractor all relevant obligations of this Agreement.

ARTICLE 3 — DELIVERABLES AND ACCEPTANCE

3.1 Delivery. The CRO shall deliver each deliverable in accordance with the schedule and in the format set forth in the applicable Work Order.

3.2 Acceptance Period. The Sponsor shall have a period of twenty (20) business days following delivery of each deliverable to review the deliverable and notify the CRO in writing of acceptance or rejection. Rejection shall be accompanied by a detailed description of the alleged non-conformity.

3.3 Cure of Non-Conformity. The CRO shall correct rejected deliverables at no additional charge within fifteen (15) business days. After two (2) cycles of cure, the Sponsor may, at its option, (a) accept the deliverable with an equitable Fee reduction, (b) terminate the affected Work Order, or (c) require the CRO to engage at the CRO's expense a third party reasonably acceptable to the Sponsor to complete the deliverable.

3.4 No Deemed Acceptance. There shall be no deemed acceptance of any deliverable.

3.5 Regulatory-Quality Deliverables. Where a deliverable will be submitted to a Regulatory Authority, the CRO shall ensure that the deliverable meets the quality standards required for regulatory submission and is consistent with the Protocol and GCP.

ARTICLE 4 — FEES AND PAYMENT

4.1 Fees. The Sponsor shall pay the CRO the Fees set forth in each Work Order. Fees may be calculated on a fixed-fee, milestone-based, time-and-materials, or pass-through basis as set forth in the Work Order.

4.2 Annual Aggregate Reference. The aggregate annual Fees payable by the Sponsor across all then-active Work Orders as of the Effective Date is approximately Three Hundred Sixty Thousand United States Dollars ($360,000), included for reference only.

4.3 Pass-Through Costs. The Sponsor shall reimburse the CRO for pass-through costs (such as Site investigator fees, IRB fees, central laboratory fees, and patient stipends) at cost, accompanied by reasonable documentation. The Sponsor's prior written approval shall be required for any pass-through cost in excess of the budget set forth in the Work Order.

4.4 Change Orders. Any change to the scope, Protocol, schedule, or Fees set forth in a Work Order shall be documented in a written change order signed by both Parties. The Parties acknowledge that Protocol amendments are common in clinical research and shall be reflected in change orders that adjust the Fees and timeline as appropriate.

4.5 Invoicing. The CRO shall invoice the Sponsor monthly in arrears for Services performed and pass-through costs incurred, subject to any milestone-based or fixed-fee provisions in the Work Order.

4.6 Payment Terms. All undisputed invoices shall be due and payable within forty-five (45) days of the date of invoice.

4.7 Disputed Invoices. The Sponsor may withhold payment of any disputed amount until the dispute is resolved.

4.8 Audit Right. The Sponsor shall have the right, upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, to audit the CRO's records for any Services billed on a time-and-materials basis or any pass-through costs.

4.9 Taxes. Fees are exclusive of all taxes other than taxes imposed on the CRO's net income.

5.2 Renewal. This Agreement shall automatically renew for successive one (1) year renewal terms unless either Party provides written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the then-current term.

5.3 Sponsor Termination for Convenience. The Sponsor may terminate this Agreement, or any Work Order, for convenience at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice. 6.1 Key Personnel. Each Work Order shall identify the Key Personnel of the CRO assigned to the Clinical Trial, including the project manager, the lead clinical research associate, and the responsible biostatistician.

6.2 No Replacement Without Consent. The CRO shall not replace any Key Personnel without the Sponsor's prior written consent except in case of death, disability, or departure from the CRO. 6.3 Removal on Sponsor Request. The Sponsor may, at any time, request that the CRO remove any individual personnel from the Clinical Trial. The CRO shall comply within five (5) business days.

6.4 GCP Training. The CRO shall ensure that all personnel performing the Services have completed GCP training appropriate to their role and have read the Protocol.

6.5 Investigator Selection. The CRO shall recommend Investigators to the Sponsor based on the criteria set forth in the Work Order. The Sponsor retains the right to approve or reject any proposed Investigator and to terminate any Investigator's involvement in the Clinical Trial.

ARTICLE 7 — TRIAL DATA, SUBJECT PRIVACY, AND REGULATORY COMPLIANCE

7.1 Ownership of Trial Data. As between the Parties, the Sponsor shall retain all right, title, and interest in and to all Trial Data, including all case report forms, source documents, laboratory results, imaging, electronic data, biological samples (subject to the consent obtained from each subject), and any other data generated in or arising from the Clinical Trial.

7.2 Permitted Uses. The CRO shall use Trial Data solely as necessary to perform the Services. The CRO shall not (a) use Trial Data for any other purpose; (b) sell, lease, or rent Trial Data; (c) use Trial Data to train any machine learning model or for any commercial product; (d) publish any results from the Trial Data without the Sponsor's prior written consent; or (e) disclose Trial Data to any third party except as expressly permitted herein.

7.3 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance. To the extent the CRO uses electronic systems to capture, store, or process Trial Data, the CRO shall ensure that such systems comply with 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures), including validation, audit trails, electronic signatures, and access controls.

7.4 HIPAA. To the extent the Trial Data includes Protected Health Information from United States subjects, the CRO is a "business associate" of the Sponsor under HIPAA, and the Business Associate Agreement attached as Exhibit A governs the CRO's handling of PHI.

7.5 Subject Consent. The CRO shall ensure that each Investigator obtains and documents informed consent from each subject in accordance with 21 C.F.R. Part 50 and applicable IRB requirements. The CRO shall not disclose subject identifiable information except to the Sponsor, the Regulatory Authorities, the IRB, and other authorized parties.

7.6 Pharmacovigilance and Adverse Event Reporting. The CRO shall conduct pharmacovigilance activities in accordance with the Protocol and applicable Regulatory Authority requirements. The CRO shall report serious adverse events and suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions to the Sponsor without delay and within the timeframes required by the applicable regulatory framework.

7.7 Regulatory Inspections. The CRO shall cooperate fully with any FDA inspection, foreign Regulatory Authority inspection, Sponsor audit, or IRB inspection of the CRO's facilities, records, or systems related to the Clinical Trial.

7.8 Sponsor Audit Right. The Sponsor shall have the right, upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice (or shorter notice in case of a regulatory inspection or for-cause audit), to audit the CRO's compliance with this Agreement, GCP, and applicable laws.

7.9 Data Security. The CRO shall implement and maintain administrative, physical, and technical safeguards designed to protect Trial Data, including encryption in transit (TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (AES-256), role-based access controls, multi-factor authentication, annual third-party penetration testing, and a documented information security program.

7.10 Breach Notification. The CRO shall notify the Sponsor of any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to or disclosure of Trial Data within twenty-four (24) hours of discovery, with regular updates until the incident is resolved.

7.11 Cross-Border Data Transfer. To the extent the Clinical Trial involves the transfer of personal data across borders, the CRO shall comply with all applicable cross-border transfer requirements (including the EU Standard Contractual Clauses where applicable).

7.12 Return of Trial Data. Upon completion of the relevant Clinical Trial or upon the Sponsor's earlier written request, the CRO shall transfer all Trial Data to the Sponsor in the format and on the timeline specified by the Sponsor, and shall destroy all copies of Trial Data in its possession (except as required by law for the CRO's records retention obligations).

ARTICLE 8 — INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS

8.1 Background IP. As between the Parties, each Party shall retain all right, title, and interest in and to its respective Background IP. The CRO's Background IP includes the CRO's project management methodologies, electronic data capture system, biostatistical software, monitoring tools, and proprietary databases.

8.2 Sponsor Ownership of Trial Data and Inventions. The Sponsor shall own all Trial Data, all inventions arising from the Clinical Trial that relate to the Investigational Product or its use, all data analyses related to the Investigational Product, and all results of the Clinical Trial. 8.3 License to Background IP. To the extent any deliverable incorporates the CRO's Background IP, the CRO hereby grants the Sponsor a perpetual, irrevocable, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use such Background IP solely as embedded in the deliverable.

8.4 Publication Rights. The Sponsor retains the exclusive right to publish or to authorize publication of the results of any Clinical Trial. Investigators may publish only in accordance with the publication provisions of the Investigator Agreement, which the CRO shall negotiate at the Sponsor's direction.

8.5 No Implied Licenses. Except for the limited rights expressly granted in this Article 8, neither Party grants any rights or licenses to the other Party.

ARTICLE 9 — CONFIDENTIALITY

9.2 Sponsor's Confidential Information. 9.3 Compelled Disclosure. The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to the extent required by law, court order, or regulator with examination authority, provided that the Receiving Party gives the Disclosing Party prompt written notice (where legally permitted).

9.4 Survival. The obligations in this Article 9 shall survive any expiration or termination of this Agreement for a period of seven (7) years, except that obligations with respect to Trial Data, the Protocol, and trade secrets shall survive for so long as such information remains protected under applicable law.

13.1 Termination for Material Breach. Either Party may terminate this Agreement, or any Work Order, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice if the other Party commits a material breach and fails to cure within the notice period.

SOFTWARE AS A SERVICE SUBSCRIPTION AGREEMENT

This Software as a Service Subscription Agreement (this "Agreement") is made and entered into as of August 15, 2024 (the "Effective Date"), by and between Streamline Cloud Inc., a Delaware corporation having its principal place of business at 4621 Mission Avenue South, Minneapolis, Minnesota 806 ("Provider"), and The Board of Regents of the Texas State University System, a state agency and instrumentality of the State of Texas, having its principal administrative office at 601 Colorado Street, Suite 200, Austin, Texas 78701 ("Customer"). RECITALS

ARTICLE 4 — SUBSCRIPTION FEES AND PAYMENT

4.1 Subscription Fees. In consideration of the Services to be provided by Provider, Customer shall pay an annual Subscription Fee of One Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars ($150,000), which entitles Customer to provision the Platform to up to five thousand (5,000) Authorized Users who are enrolled students of Customer's constituent institutions. 4.2 Payment Terms. All Subscription Fees shall be due and payable in United States Dollars within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice (the "Due Date"). Customer shall make all payments by electronic funds transfer to the account designated by Provider in writing. The Parties acknowledge that, as Customer is a state agency, payment is subject to applicable Texas state appropriations law and the Texas Prompt Payment Act, Chapter 2251 of the Texas Government Code.

4.3 Excess Usage. If Customer's usage of the Platform exceeds five thousand (5,000) Authorized Users in any Subscription Year, Customer shall pay an additional fee of Thirty United States Dollars ($30) per Authorized User per Subscription Year for each Authorized User in excess of the included allotment, calculated based on the peak number of concurrent provisioned Authorized Users during the Subscription Year. Such excess usage fees shall be invoiced at the end of the applicable Subscription Year and shall be due within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice.

4.4 Late Payments. Any undisputed Subscription Fees not paid by the Due Date shall accrue interest at a rate equal to the lesser of (a) one percent (1.0%) per month or (b) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, in each case calculated from the original Due Date until the date of actual payment. ARTICLE 5 — TERM AND RENEWAL

5.1 Initial Term. The initial term of this Agreement (the "Initial Term") shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue for a period of two (2) years, unless earlier terminated in accordance with Article 13.

5.2 Renewal Terms. 5.4 Customer Termination for Convenience. Notwithstanding Section 5.2, Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience by providing Provider with at least ninety (90) days' prior written notice, with such termination to take effect at the end of an Academic Term to minimize disruption to Authorized Users.

ARTICLE 6 — SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SUPPORT

6.1 Uptime Commitment. Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to make the Platform available with a Monthly Uptime Percentage of at least 99.9% during Academic Terms, calculated as: (Total Minutes in Month - Excluded Minutes - Downtime Minutes) / (Total Minutes in Month - Excluded Minutes), expressed as a percentage. During academic break periods (defined as the period between Academic Terms when fewer than ten percent (10%) of provisioned Authorized Users are actively using the Platform), Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain availability but shall not be subject to the 99.9% commitment.

6.2 Excluded Downtime. The following shall not be counted as Downtime for purposes of calculating Monthly Uptime Percentage: (a) scheduled maintenance windows announced at least seventy-two (72) hours in advance, which shall not exceed eight (8) hours per calendar month and shall be scheduled outside of peak usage hours; (b) emergency maintenance required to address security vulnerabilities, with as much advance notice as is reasonably practicable; (c) downtime caused by Customer's acts or omissions, including misconfiguration of Customer's identity provider; (d) downtime caused by force majeure events; and (e) downtime caused by failures of third-party services or networks outside Provider's reasonable control.

6.3 Service Credits. If the Monthly Uptime Percentage during an Academic Term falls below 99.9%, Customer shall be entitled to receive service credits as follows: (a) below 99.9% but at or above 99.5%: a service credit equal to five percent (5%) of one-twelfth (1/12) of the annual Subscription Fee; (b) below 99.5% but at or above 99.0%: a service credit equal to ten percent (10%) of one-twelfth (1/12) of the annual Subscription Fee; (c) below 99.0%: a service credit equal to twenty-five percent (25%) of one-twelfth (1/12) of the annual Subscription Fee. Service credits shall be Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for failures to meet the Service Level Agreement, except that two (2) or more consecutive months of SLA failures during Academic Terms shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement entitling Customer to terminate for cause pursuant to Section 13.2 without further notice.

6.4 Service Credit Procedure. To claim a service credit, Customer shall submit a written request to Provider within thirty (30) days following the end of the affected month, specifying the basis for the claim. Provider shall apply approved service credits to the next subsequent invoice. Service credits shall not be paid in cash and shall not exceed in the aggregate twenty-five percent (25%) of the annual Subscription Fee for any Subscription Year.

6.5 Support Services. Provider shall provide the following Support Services to Customer's designated administrators during the Subscription Term: (a) twenty-four hours per day, seven days per week ("24x7") access to a knowledge base, online help center, and self-service ticketing portal; (b) email support with a target initial response time of four (4) business hours for issues affecting the production environment; (c) telephone support during Provider's standard business hours of 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Pacific Time, Monday through Friday, excluding Provider's published holidays; and (d) emergency on-call support for Severity 1 incidents (defined as a complete outage of the Platform affecting all Authorized Users) with a target initial response time of one (1) hour, twenty-four hours per day, seven days per week.

6.6 Severity Levels. Provider shall categorize support issues using the following severity levels: Severity 1 (complete production outage), Severity 2 (significant degradation affecting a substantial portion of users), Severity 3 (limited functionality issue with a workaround), and Severity 4 (general inquiry or feature request). Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to resolve Severity 1 issues within four (4) hours, Severity 2 issues within one (1) business day, Severity 3 issues within five (5) business days, and Severity 4 issues in accordance with Provider's standard product roadmap.

6.7 Maintenance Windows. Provider shall conduct routine maintenance of the Platform during a standard maintenance window of Sunday from 10:00 p.m. to 2:00 a.m. Pacific Time. Provider shall provide Customer with at least seventy-two (72) hours' advance notice of any maintenance that is expected to result in service interruption during the standard maintenance window. Maintenance scheduled outside the standard window shall require at least five (5) business days' advance notice except in the case of emergency maintenance.

ARTICLE 7 — CUSTOMER DATA AND PRIVACY

7.1 Ownership of Customer Data. As between the Parties, Customer shall retain all right, title, and interest in and to Customer Data, including all Student Data. Provider acknowledges that Customer Data is the exclusive property of Customer and that Provider has no right, title, or interest in Customer Data except for the limited license set forth in Section 7.2.

7.2 License to Process. Customer hereby grants to Provider a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free license to access, store, process, transmit, and display Customer Data solely as necessary to provide the Services to Customer in accordance with this Agreement and the Documentation. Provider shall not use Customer Data for any other purpose, including without limitation product improvement, machine learning model training, marketing, or sale to third parties, except as expressly permitted by Customer in writing.

7.3 FERPA Designation. The Parties acknowledge that, in providing the Services, Provider is acting as a "school official" with "legitimate educational interests" in the meaning of FERPA, 34 C.F.R. § 99.31(a)(1)(i)(B). Provider shall (a) use Student Data only for the purpose of providing the Services to Customer; (b) not disclose Student Data to any third party except as necessary to provide the Services and only after such third party has agreed in writing to comply with FERPA's restrictions on the use and re-disclosure of Student Data; and (c) maintain the confidentiality of Student Data in accordance with FERPA and this Agreement.

7.4 Data Security. Provider shall implement and maintain reasonable and appropriate administrative, physical, and technical safeguards designed to protect Customer Data against unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, and destruction. Such safeguards shall include, at a minimum, (a) encryption of Customer Data in transit using Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 or higher; (b) encryption of Customer Data at rest using AES-256 or equivalent; (c) role-based access controls limiting access to Customer Data to Provider personnel with a need to know; (d) annual third-party penetration testing of the Platform; (e) maintenance of SOC 2 Type II certification; and (f) a documented information security program reviewed and updated at least annually.

7.5 Breach Notification. ARTICLE 7 — SUBSCRIBER DATA, PRIVACY, AND CONSENT

This is the most important article in the Agreement. If anything in it conflicts with anything elsewhere, this Article 7 wins.

7.1 You own Subscriber Data. You own all Subscriber Data. We do not own it. We do not get a license to use it beyond what Section 7.2 says.

7.2 Why we touch Subscriber Data. You give us permission to host, store, process, and use Subscriber Data only as needed to provide the PulseLoop Platform to you — sending the messages you compose, recording delivery and engagement events, and producing analytics for you. We will not use Subscriber Data for any other purpose unless you give us specific written permission.

7.3 No selling, no AI training. We will not sell Subscriber Data. We will not share Subscriber Data with anyone except the subprocessors listed in Section 7.10. We will not use Subscriber Data, your campaign content, or your engagement metrics to train any artificial intelligence model unless you give us specific written permission for a specific project, and you can say no without affecting any of your other rights.

7.4 Consent is on you. You promise that for every Subscriber in the PulseLoop Platform, you have a lawful basis to send them marketing messages (express opt-in for SMS and for email subscribers in jurisdictions that require it; CAN-SPAM-compliant opt-in plus working opt-out for other email subscribers; CASL-compliant consent for Canadian Subscribers). You promise to honor unsubscribe and opt-out requests promptly. Our system supports unsubscribe links in every email and a STOP keyword for SMS — but the legal obligation to comply is yours.

7.5 Sub-processor sync of opt-outs. When a Subscriber unsubscribes through one of our links, we mark them as unsubscribed in your account immediately and we sync the unsubscribe to your connected e-commerce platform on a best-effort basis. You are responsible for ensuring your other systems (CRM, support tools, post-purchase tools) honor the unsubscribe.

7.6 Data Processing Addendum. The DPA at pulseloop.com/dpa is part of this Agreement and explains in detail how we handle personal data on your behalf. If applicable laws (like the EU Standard Contractual Clauses, the UK International Data Transfer Agreement, the CPRA, the Virginia CDPA, the Colorado Privacy Act, the Connecticut Data Privacy Act, the Utah Consumer Privacy Act, or any other state privacy law) require additional terms, the DPA controls. You are the controller of personal data; we are the processor.

7.7 Security. We protect Subscriber Data with: (a) encryption in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher; (b) encryption at rest using AES-256; (c) role-based access controls; (d) annual third-party penetration testing; (e) annual SOC 2 Type II audits; and (f) a documented information security program reviewed annually.

7.8 Breach. If we discover a security incident that compromises Subscriber Data, we will tell you in writing without undue delay and in any case within seventy-two (72) hours of discovery. The notice will describe what we know about the incident, the data involved, and what we are doing about it. We will help you investigate. If the incident was caused by something we did wrong and triggers state breach notification requirements, we will reimburse you for the reasonable cost of the required notifications.

7.9 Data residency. We store and process Subscriber Data in the United States. If you need a different region, talk to us — additional fees may apply and the available regions are limited.

7.10 Subprocessors. We use a small list of subprocessors to operate the PulseLoop Platform. The current list is at pulseloop.com/subprocessors and includes (as of the Start Date) (a) our cloud hosting provider; (b) our email sending provider; (c) our SMS provider; (d) our error tracking provider; and (e) our customer support tool. We give you fifteen (15) days notice before adding or changing a subprocessor that handles Subscriber Data, and you can object on reasonable security grounds. If we cannot resolve your objection, you can terminate this Agreement and get a prorated refund of unused prepaid fees.

7.11 Data return and deletion. When this Agreement ends, you have sixty (60) days to export Subscriber Data and your campaign history using our self-service export tool at no charge. After that, we delete Subscriber Data from our production systems within thirty (30) days, with backup deletion completed within ninety (90) days as part of our normal retention cycle. We will give you a written certification of deletion if you ask.

7.12 Subscriber rights requests. If a Subscriber asks you to delete or export their personal data under an applicable privacy law, you can use our self-service tools in the dashboard to honor that request. We will help you respond to Subscriber rights requests on a reasonable best-effort basis.

The Auditor shall not perform any non-audit services for the Company without the prior written approval of the Audit Committee, which approval shall be sought in accordance with the Audit Committee's pre-approval policies and the auditor independence rules.

2.6 Communications with the Audit Committee. The Auditor shall communicate directly with the Audit Committee on matters required to be communicated by PCAOB standards, including significant accounting policies and practices, critical audit matters, significant deficiencies and material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting, instances of fraud or illegal acts, disagreements with management, and other matters required to be communicated to the Audit Committee.

3.2 No Acceptance Mechanic for Audit Reports. The Parties acknowledge that the Auditor's reports reflect the Auditor's professional judgment and are not subject to acceptance by the Company. ARTICLE 4 — FEES AND PAYMENT

4.2 Annual Aggregate Reference. The aggregate annual Fees payable by the Company across all then-active Engagement Letters as of the Effective Date is approximately Four Hundred Eighty Thousand United States Dollars ($480,000), included for reference only.

4.3 Audit Committee Pre-Approval. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, no Fees shall be paid to the Auditor for any service that has not been pre-approved by the Audit Committee in accordance with the Audit Committee's pre-approval policies.

4.4 Out-of-Scope Work. Any work performed at the Company's request that is outside the scope of an Engagement Letter shall require an amendment to the Engagement Letter and prior approval by the Audit Committee.

4.5 Expenses. Reasonable travel and out-of-pocket expenses incurred by the Auditor in connection with the Services shall be reimbursed by the Company at cost without markup, accompanied by reasonable documentation, and subject to the Company's then-current expense policies.

4.6 Payment Terms. All undisputed invoices shall be due and payable within forty-five (45) days of the date of invoice.

4.7 Disputed Invoices. The Company may withhold payment of any disputed amount until the dispute is resolved. The Auditor shall not impose any late fee, interest charge, or work stoppage with respect to any amount in good-faith dispute. The Auditor shall not, however, suspend or delay the issuance of any audit report on account of a fee dispute, given the regulatory and reporting obligations of the Company.

4.8 Taxes. Fees are exclusive of all taxes other than taxes imposed on the Auditor's net income.

ARTICLE 5 — TERM AND TERMINATION

5.1 Initial Term. This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue for a period of one (1) years, unless earlier terminated in accordance with Article 13. 6.1 Engagement Partner. Each Engagement Letter shall identify the lead audit engagement partner who is responsible for the engagement. 6.2 Concurring Partner. Each Engagement Letter for a Public Company Audit shall also identify the concurring audit engagement partner, who shall conduct the engagement quality review required by PCAOB Auditing Standard 1220. The concurring partner is also subject to the five-year rotation requirement.

7.1 Company Cooperation. 7.5 Confidentiality of Company Information. The Auditor shall hold all Company Materials and other non-public information about the Company in strict confidence and shall use such information solely for the purpose of performing the Services. The Auditor shall not disclose such information to any third party except (a) to its own personnel who have a need to know in connection with the audit, (b) to the PCAOB, the SEC, or other regulatory authorities as required by law or PCAOB standards, (c) to a successor auditor as required or permitted by the AICPA Code of Professional Conduct, or (d) as the Company may otherwise authorize in writing.

7.6 Data Security. The Auditor shall implement and maintain reasonable administrative, physical, and technical safeguards designed to protect Company Materials against unauthorized access, including encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access controls, and a documented information security program reviewed annually.

This Master Subscription Agreement (this "Agreement") is made and entered into as of October 21, 2024 (the "Effective Date"), by and between Lighthouse Cloud Technologies, Inc., a Delaware corporation having its principal place of business at 1828 Mission Drive, Raleigh, North Carolina 940 ("Provider"), and Lakeshore Regional Health System, a Michigan non-profit hospital system having its principal place of business at 1 Lakeshore Health Drive, Grand Rapids, Michigan 49503 ("Customer"). Provider and Customer may each be referred to as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties."

This Agreement is intentionally a Master Agreement only. It does not, by itself, obligate Customer to purchase any Subscription, Module, or Professional Services. The specific Subscription Modules, Authorized Sites, Authorized Users, Subscription Fees, Subscription Term dates, Service Levels, and any custom terms applicable to a particular engagement shall be set forth in one or more Order Forms executed by both Parties from time to time and incorporated by reference into this Agreement (each, an "Order Form"). In the event of any conflict between this Agreement and an Order Form, the Order Form shall control as to the matters expressly addressed therein.

ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS

1.1 "Affiliate" means, with respect to any entity, any other entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with such entity, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting securities or membership interests of such entity.

1.2 "Authorized Site" means a hospital, clinic, ambulatory surgery center, physician practice, or other healthcare facility owned, operated, or managed by Customer or its Affiliates and identified on an Order Form.

1.3 "Authorized User" means an individual employee, contractor, medical staff member, or other workforce member of Customer or an Authorized Site who is authorized by Customer to access and use the Platform pursuant to the rights granted on an Order Form.

1.4 "BAA" means the Business Associate Agreement attached hereto as Exhibit A and executed simultaneously with this Agreement.

1.5 "Customer Data" means all electronic data, content, records, and other information that is uploaded to, transmitted through, processed by, or stored within the Platform by or on behalf of Customer, an Authorized Site, or any Authorized User in connection with Customer's use of the Services, including without limitation Protected Health Information.

1.6 "HIPAA" means the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996, as amended by the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act ("HITECH") and the regulations promulgated thereunder at 45 C.F.R. Parts 160 and 164.

1.7 "Module" means a discrete functional component of the Platform (such as the inpatient EHR Module, the ambulatory EHR Module, the revenue cycle Module, the patient portal Module, the analytics Module, or the population health Module) as identified on an Order Form.

1.8 "Order Form" has the meaning set forth in the preamble.

1.9 "Platform" means Provider's hosted electronic health record and clinical workflow software-as-a-service platform, including all Modules made available to Customer under one or more Order Forms.

1.10 "Professional Services" means implementation, configuration, data migration, integration, training, optimization, and other professional services provided by Provider under a Statement of Work.

1.11 "Protected Health Information" or "PHI" has the meaning set forth in 45 C.F.R. § 160.103 and includes any individually identifiable health information transmitted, maintained, or processed through the Platform on Customer's behalf.

1.12 "Service Level Agreement" or "SLA" means the service level commitments set forth in the applicable Order Form or the Service Level Exhibit attached thereto.

1.13 "Statement of Work" or "SOW" means a written document signed by both Parties describing Professional Services to be provided by Provider, which is incorporated by reference into this Agreement.

1.14 "Subscription" means Customer's right to access and use a specified set of Modules at specified Authorized Sites for a specified Subscription Term, in each case as set forth on an Order Form.

1.15 "Subscription Fees" means the fees payable by Customer to Provider for a Subscription, as set forth on the applicable Order Form.

1.16 "Subscription Term" means the period during which a Subscription is in effect, as set forth on the applicable Order Form.

ARTICLE 2 — SUBSCRIPTION AND LICENSE

2.1 Provision of Services. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the applicable Order Form, and Customer's compliance therewith, Provider shall make the Modules identified on each Order Form available to Customer and the Authorized Sites and Authorized Users specified on such Order Form during the applicable Subscription Term, in accordance with the Service Level Agreement and the Documentation.

2.2 License Grant. Provider hereby grants to Customer, during each Subscription Term, a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable right and license to access and use the Modules identified on the applicable Order Form for the internal healthcare operations of Customer and the Authorized Sites set forth on such Order Form. The scope of the license, including the maximum number of Authorized Users, the included Authorized Sites, and any usage caps, is as expressly set forth on the applicable Order Form.

2.3 Restrictions. Except as expressly permitted in this Agreement and the applicable Order Form, Customer shall not (a) modify, adapt, or create derivative works based on the Platform; (b) sublicense, rent, sell, or otherwise commercially exploit access to the Platform; (c) reverse engineer the Platform; (d) use the Platform to build a competing product; or (e) use the Platform in any manner not authorized by the applicable Order Form.

2.4 Affiliates and Authorized Sites. Customer's Affiliates may receive the benefit of Subscriptions only if such Affiliates are identified as Authorized Sites on the applicable Order Form. Customer shall remain responsible for the acts and omissions of its Affiliates and Authorized Sites in connection with their use of the Platform and for compliance by such Affiliates and Authorized Sites with this Agreement.

2.5 Suspension. Provider may suspend Customer's access to the Platform, in whole or in part, upon prior written notice if Provider reasonably determines that (a) Customer's use poses an immediate and material security risk; (b) Customer has materially breached the license restrictions in Section 2.3 and failed to cure within ten (10) business days of written notice; or (c) suspension is required by law. Provider shall not suspend access to clinical Modules during a clinical event or outage in a manner that would foreseeably endanger patient care, except where required by law.

ARTICLE 3 — IMPLEMENTATION AND PROFESSIONAL SERVICES

3.1 Statements of Work. Professional Services shall be provided under one or more SOWs, each of which shall specify the scope, deliverables, timeline, acceptance criteria, fees, and any project-specific terms. Each SOW shall be deemed incorporated into this Agreement upon execution by both Parties.

3.2 No Implementation by Default. This Agreement does not, by itself, obligate Provider to perform any Professional Services. Implementation, data migration, integration with Customer's existing systems, training, and any other Professional Services shall be performed only pursuant to a duly executed SOW.

3.3 Change Orders. Any change to the scope of Professional Services described in an SOW shall be documented in a written change order signed by both Parties. Change orders may result in adjustments to fees, deliverables, or schedules, as set forth therein.

3.4 Customer Responsibilities. Customer acknowledges that timely completion of Professional Services depends on Customer's cooperation, including timely access to systems, data, and personnel. Provider shall not be responsible for delays in Professional Services attributable to Customer.

ARTICLE 4 — SUBSCRIPTION FEES AND PAYMENT

4.1 Fees. Customer shall pay Provider the Subscription Fees, Professional Services fees, and any other amounts set forth on the applicable Order Form or SOW. Except as expressly set forth on an Order Form, Subscription Fees are payable annually in advance.

4.2 Annual Aggregate. The annual aggregate Subscription Fees payable by Customer across all then-active Order Forms as of the Effective Date is Seven Hundred Twenty Thousand United States Dollars ($720,000), which figure is included in this Agreement for reference only and shall be updated by reference to the Order Forms then in effect from time to time.

4.3 Payment Terms. Unless otherwise set forth on an Order Form, all undisputed invoices shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice. Late payments shall accrue interest at the lesser of one percent (1%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law.

4.4 Disputed Invoices. If Customer in good faith disputes any portion of an invoice, Customer shall notify Provider in writing of the dispute within fifteen (15) business days of receipt, identifying the disputed amount and the basis for the dispute. Customer shall pay all undisputed amounts on time. The Parties shall negotiate in good faith to resolve the dispute.

4.5 Taxes. Subscription Fees and Professional Services fees are exclusive of all taxes other than taxes imposed on Provider's net income. Customer shall be responsible for all applicable taxes, except to the extent Customer is exempt and provides Provider with a valid exemption certificate.

ARTICLE 5 — TERM AND RENEWAL

5.1 Agreement Term. This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in effect so long as any Order Form executed under it remains in effect, unless earlier terminated in accordance with Article 13.

5.2 Subscription Term. The Subscription Term for each Subscription shall be as set forth on the applicable Order Form. Each Subscription shall automatically renew for successive renewal terms equal in length to the initial Subscription Term unless either Party provides written notice of non-renewal to the other Party at least one hundred eighty (180) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Subscription Term.

5.3 Effect of Order Form Expiration. Expiration or termination of an individual Order Form shall not, by itself, terminate this Agreement or any other Order Form, unless expressly stated otherwise in the affected Order Form.

5.4 Fee Adjustments at Renewal. Provider may adjust Subscription Fees for any renewal Subscription Term by providing written notice of the adjusted fees to Customer at least one hundred twenty (120) days prior to the start of the renewal Subscription Term. Any adjustment shall not exceed five percent (5%) above the Subscription Fees in effect during the immediately preceding Subscription Year.

ARTICLE 6 — SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SUPPORT

6.1 Service Levels. The Service Level commitments applicable to each Module — including uptime targets, support response times, and service credits — shall be set forth in the Service Level Exhibit to the applicable Order Form. The Parties acknowledge that different Modules may carry different Service Levels reflecting their criticality to patient care.

6.2 Clinical Module Standard. Notwithstanding Section 6.1, all Modules that touch direct clinical workflows (inpatient EHR, ambulatory EHR, computerized provider order entry, and medication administration) shall be subject to a default uptime commitment of at least 99.9% measured monthly, excluding scheduled maintenance and force majeure events, regardless of whether such commitment is restated on the Order Form.

6.3 Support Tiers. Provider shall provide the support tier specified on the applicable Order Form. Standard support includes (a) twenty-four hours per day, seven days per week access to Provider's online help center; (b) email and telephone support during defined business hours; and (c) twenty-four hours per day, seven days per week emergency on-call support for Severity 1 incidents affecting clinical Modules with a target initial response time of one (1) hour.

6.4 Service Credits. Service credits for failure to meet the Service Levels shall be Customer's sole and exclusive monetary remedy for such failure, except that two (2) or more consecutive months of failure to meet the clinical Module uptime commitment under Section 6.2 shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement entitling Customer to terminate the affected Order Form for cause.

ARTICLE 7 — CUSTOMER DATA, PRIVACY, AND HIPAA

7.1 Ownership of Customer Data. As between the Parties, Customer shall retain all right, title, and interest in and to Customer Data, including all PHI. Provider acknowledges that Customer Data is the exclusive property of Customer.

7.2 Business Associate Status. The Parties acknowledge that, in providing the Services, Provider shall be acting as a "business associate" of Customer, as that term is defined under HIPAA. The BAA attached hereto as Exhibit A is incorporated by reference and constitutes the binding Business Associate Agreement between the Parties. In the event of a conflict between this Article 7 and the BAA with respect to PHI, the BAA shall control.

7.3 Permitted Uses. Provider shall use and disclose Customer Data, including PHI, only as permitted by HIPAA, the BAA, this Agreement, and the applicable Order Form. Provider shall not use Customer Data for any other purpose, including without limitation product improvement, machine learning model training, marketing, or sale to third parties, except as expressly permitted by Customer in writing.

7.4 Security. Provider shall implement and maintain administrative, physical, and technical safeguards designed to comply with the HIPAA Security Rule (45 C.F.R. Part 164, Subpart C), including without limitation (a) encryption of PHI in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher; (b) encryption of PHI at rest using AES-256; (c) role-based access controls aligned with the Authorized Site and Authorized User structure on each Order Form; (d) annual third-party penetration testing; (e) maintenance of HITRUST CSF certification or equivalent; and (f) a documented information security program reviewed and updated at least annually.

7.5 Breach Notification. Provider shall notify Customer in writing of any "Breach" of "Unsecured Protected Health Information" (as both terms are defined under 45 C.F.R. § 164.402) without unreasonable delay and in any event within the timeframe set forth in the BAA, which shall not exceed seventy-two (72) hours of Provider's discovery of such Breach.

7.6 Right to Audit. Once per calendar year, upon at least sixty (60) days prior written notice, Customer (or a third-party assessor engaged by Customer and bound by reasonable confidentiality obligations) shall have the right to audit Provider's compliance with this Article 7 and the BAA, at Customer's expense. Customer shall conduct any audit during normal business hours, in a manner that does not unreasonably interfere with Provider's operations, and in compliance with Provider's reasonable security protocols. The frequency of audits may be increased without limitation following a Security Incident or upon the request of any regulator with jurisdiction over Customer.

7.7 Subprocessors. Provider shall maintain a list of subprocessors that have access to PHI on Provider's Customer Trust Portal, which list is incorporated by reference into the BAA. Provider shall provide Customer with at least thirty (30) days prior written notice of any addition or change to a subprocessor that has access to PHI. Customer may object to any new or changed subprocessor on reasonable security or compliance grounds. If the Parties cannot resolve Customer's objection in good faith, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form for cause and receive a prorated refund of any prepaid Subscription Fees.

7.8 Regulator Cooperation. Provider shall cooperate with any audit, inquiry, or investigation by the Department of Health and Human Services Office for Civil Rights, any state attorney general, or any other regulator with jurisdiction over Customer's handling of PHI. Provider shall make available to Customer such information as Customer may reasonably require to respond to any such regulatory inquiry.

7.9 Data Residency. Provider shall store and process Customer Data within data centers physically located in the contiguous United States. Provider shall not transfer Customer Data outside of the United States without Customer's prior written consent.

7.10 Data Return and Deletion. Upon expiration or termination of an Order Form for any reason, Provider shall, at Customer's election: (a) make Customer Data attributable to such Order Form available for export by Customer in a commercially reasonable, machine-readable format for a period of one hundred eighty (180) days following expiration or termination; or (b) permanently delete such Customer Data from Provider's production systems within thirty (30) days of expiration or termination, with backup deletion to follow in accordance with Provider's standard backup retention schedule.

As between the Parties, Provider shall retain all right, title, and interest in and to the Platform, the Modules, the Documentation, and all related Intellectual Property Rights, including without limitation any modifications, enhancements, derivative works, or improvements thereto. Customer hereby grants Provider a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, worldwide license to use such Feedback to improve the Platform, provided that Provider shall not use any Customer Data, including PHI, in connection with Feedback.

ARTICLE 9 — CONFIDENTIALITY

9.1 Confidentiality Obligations. Each Party agrees to (a) hold the other Party's Confidential Information in strict confidence; (b) use the other Party's Confidential Information solely for the purposes of this Agreement; (c) not disclose the other Party's Confidential Information to any third party except to its employees, contractors, and advisors who have a legitimate need to know and who are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as those set forth in this Article 9; and (d) protect the other Party's Confidential Information using the same degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential information of similar importance, but in no event less than reasonable care.

9.2 Exclusions. The obligations in Section 9.1 shall not apply to information that the Receiving Party can demonstrate (a) was already known to it without obligation of confidentiality; (b) was independently developed without use of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information; (c) was rightfully received from a third party without obligation of confidentiality; or (d) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the Receiving Party.

9.3 Compelled Disclosure. The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to the extent required by law or regulatory authority, provided that the Receiving Party (a) gives the Disclosing Party prompt written notice of the requirement, to the extent legally permitted; (b) cooperates with the Disclosing Party in any reasonable effort to obtain a protective order; and (c) discloses only that portion of Confidential Information that is legally required.

9.4 Survival. The obligations in this Article 9 shall survive any expiration or termination of this Agreement for a period of five (5) years, except that obligations with respect to PHI and trade secrets shall survive for so long as such information remains protected under applicable law.

13.1 Termination for Material Breach. Either Party may terminate this Agreement, an Order Form, or an SOW upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Party if the other Party commits a material breach of this Agreement, the applicable Order Form, or the applicable SOW and fails to cure such breach within the thirty (30) day notice period. 13.2 Termination for Insolvency. Either Party may terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice if the other Party (a) becomes insolvent; (b) makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors; (c) files a voluntary petition in bankruptcy; or (d) has an involuntary petition in bankruptcy filed against it that is not dismissed within sixty (60) days.

13.3 Termination for Loss of HITRUST or Regulatory Action. Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form upon written notice if (a) Provider loses or fails to maintain HITRUST CSF certification (or Customer-approved equivalent) for a period exceeding ninety (90) days; or (b) Provider becomes the subject of a final, non-appealable enforcement action by the Department of Health and Human Services Office for Civil Rights for a violation of HIPAA that materially affects Provider's ability to perform under this Agreement.

13.4 Effects of Termination. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement: (a) all rights and licenses granted hereunder shall immediately cease; (b) Customer shall pay Provider all undisputed amounts that have accrued through the effective date of termination; (c) each Party shall return or destroy the other Party's Confidential Information in accordance with Section 9; (d) Provider shall make Customer Data available for export or shall delete Customer Data in accordance with Section 7.10; and (e) the provisions of this Agreement that by their nature are intended to survive termination, including Articles 1, 7 (in part), 8, 9, 11, 12, and 14, shall so survive.

13.5 Transition Assistance. For a period of up to one hundred eighty (180) days following the effective date of expiration or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form, Provider shall provide Customer with reasonable transition assistance to facilitate Customer's migration to a successor electronic health record system, including the export of Customer Data in standard healthcare interoperability formats (HL7, FHIR, CCDA). Standard data exports shall be provided at no additional charge. Customized or scoped transition services shall be provided under a separate SOW at Provider's then-current professional services rates.

MASTER TRANSLATION AND LOCALIZATION SERVICES AGREEMENT

1.8 "Statement of Work" or "SOW" means a written document executed by both Parties describing a particular project.

1.9 "Translation Memory" or "TM" means the bilingual database of source text and target text segments built up through the translation process.
